85e2eca73081b7fb: KUALA LUMPUR: Australia-born defender Shane Lowry has been cleared by FIFA to represent Malaysia after the world governing body approved his change of international association.

According to the official FIFA Change of Association Platform, the Players' Status Chamber of the FIFA Football Tribunal yesterday (Nov 12) approved the 37-year-old Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) centre-back's switch to the FA of Malaysia (FAM).
Lowry's former associations included the FA of Ireland and Football Australia Limited.
Born in Perth, Western Australia, he represented the Republic of Ireland at Under-17 and Under-21 levels before pursuing a senior international career with Australia.
The approval ends an eligibility saga that began earlier this season when Lowry first appeared as a local player on JDT's domestic roster.

In August, Lowry, who joined the Southern Tigers from Qatari side Al Ahli in May 2021 and has fulfilled the five-year residency requirement in Malaysia, sparked debate among fans after being listed as a local player in JDT's Super League opener and Sultan Ahmad Shah Cup victory over Kuching City.

He was registered alongside Brazilian striker Bergson da Silva, Argentine winger Manuel Hidalgo and Australia-born defender Brad Tapp without the foreign-player indicators typically displayed in FAM's competition management system.
The registrations followed the Malaysian Football League's (MFL) expansion of local player squad quotas from 18 to 23 for the 2026-2027 season, increasing maximum squad sizes from 33 to 38.

However, securing local status in domestic competitions did not automatically make Lowry eligible for Harimau Malaya, with his international paperwork drawing scrutiny over conflicting timelines from FAM.
On Sept 13, when confirming FIFA clearances for Bergson and Tapp ahead of the FIFA Asean Cup in Jakarta, FAM said Lowry's eligibility was still under review in Zurich.

"The status of two other JDT players, Manuel Hidalgo and Shane Lowry, is still in the review and verification process by FIFA, and FAM is still waiting for an official decision from the world governing body," FAM said in its statement.

Four days later, following FAM's extraordinary congress on Sept 17, secretary-general Datuk Noor Azman Rahman appeared to contradict the earlier statement, saying Lowry's application had not been submitted because of fitness concerns.
"Lowry was not applied for because he is injured. It is only three players for now, and we are just waiting on the passport clearance with the relevant FA," Noor Azman said.
FAM only confirmed in late October that Lowry's application had been formally submitted to FIFA.
"Lowry's documents are complete, and we have submitted them to FIFA. We are now waiting for FIFA's approval process in the near future," Noor Azman said on Oct 27.

Although Lowry is not part of interim head coach Tan Cheng Hoe's 23-man squad in Guangdong, China, for the friendlies against China tomorrow and Yemen on Nov 17, FIFA's approval makes the veteran defender available for future Harimau Malaya selection.
Both JDT and FAM have yet to issue official statements on the development.
0cc4e4656b42c7c3: HONG KONG, Nov 13 — Stocks mostly fell today, tracking a selloff on Wall Street as traders were spooked by the downfall of Nvidia mastermind Jensen Huang.

Investors were also keeping tabs on the Middle East crisis after Donald Trump called on Vice President JD Vance to focus on domestic issues rather than negotiations with Tehran, signalling fading interest in a peace deal.

Chip titan Nvidia has been sideswiped since reports emerged that Huang — a pivotal figure in the artificial intelligence explosion in recent years — had carried on two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China.
After days of speculation, he stepped down yesterday in the face of a boardroom revolt. He will be replaced on an interim basis by chief financial officer Colette Kress.
The crisis has seen Nvidia’s share price fall about a fifth since news of the first affair broke at the end of last month.
It fell around 14 per cent after Huang’s resignation but rebounded on dip-buying to end a little more than four per cent down, while it was up one per cent in after-hours trade.

While the crisis had raised concerns about the AI boom, which had already been stuttering owing to profitability questions, observers pointed out that business would continue and Huang’s departure would not affect short-term projects already in the works.
A Republican senator said yesterday that Huang had been asked to appear before US lawmakers, as had Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who faces scrutiny over the sale of advanced chips to China.

“Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology. I am requesting that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee,” the committee’s chairman Tim Scott said on X.
The firm’s competitors benefitted, with Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices both rallying in New York, though all three markets on Wall Street ended lower.
Asia enjoyed a more positive start today but anxiety over the crisis set in as the weekend loomed.
While Tokyo and Taipei remained in positive territory at the close — albeit at lower levels — Seoul finished down one per cent.
There were also losses in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington, Manila and Mumbai. Bangkok and Jakarta rose.
London, Paris and Frankfurt opened lower.
Gauge of AI boom

“Now that he has taken the decision to resign, the question that needs asking is whether recent events matter in the context of the wider business given that Nvidia is one of the front runners in the AI trade?” wrote Michael Hewson at MCH Market Insights.

“Business is likely to continue as before and with the numbers out next week the noise around its CEO while unwelcome doesn’t change the business case for Nvidia, even if it raises some questions about its corporate governance.

“These questions are likely to continue to rumble and there is a danger that Nvidia might become collateral damage in the aftermath as Democrats take aim at a business that has aligned itself closely to the Trump administration.”

Traders were also gearing up for next week’s market debut of Anthropic, creator of the Claude chatbot, following an initial public offering that is expected to have raised more than US$60 billion (RM245 billion).

The listing is seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom can last in the face of concerns about the huge spending on data centres and software, and possible regulation following the Democratic sweep of Congress last week.
Both main oil contracts edged down today, having seen big gains the day before after Trump appeared to turn his back on a peace agreement with Iran.
“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
The comments followed a sharp drop in crude this month on optimism the president would push for a long-standing deal with Tehran after saying he would not restart military action against Iran.

Traders are also keeping an eye on currency markets after the dollar broke back above 160 yen — the first time since the start of September — on bets the Federal Reserve will keep hiking interest rates into the new year.
The greenback’s advance sparked fresh speculation that authorities will step in to support the Japanese unit. — AFP
6c81546677e5d7f7: Only a handful of NHS trusts are using the cancer app on the controversial £330 million Federated Data Platform (FDP) run by Palantir, while newly released figures raise questions about which trusts are benefiting.
Cancer 360 was designed to bring cancer patients' data from disparate spreadsheets and electronic health records into a central system, helping health professionals prioritize treatment.

Pilots began four years ago, and trusts are not charged directly for the FDP. Yet official figures put Cancer 360's uptake at just five or six trusts. Freedom of Information responses gathered by grassroots campaign group No Palantir in the NHS also reveal discrepancies between reported benefits and recorded use.

In June 2025, NHS England said that Cancer 360 "drastically cut down diagnosis times" and referred to a pilot at Chelsea and Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, which saw the proportion of patients diagnosed within 28 days climb from 72 percent to 85 percent.

The trust began trials in 2022, while working with Palantir under a £23 million contract awarded without competition, before the US firm was awarded the FDP contract in late 2023. Critics argued the FDP procurement was flawed as Palantir had developed use cases under £60 million in non-competitive contracts which were then carried over to the FDP.
Last year, NHS England said Cancer 360 served 46 registered teams and 239 active users, and processed 52,000 patients.

In June 2026, NHS England said there were five trusts using Cancer 360 as of March 2026. Of those, only two were listed as benefiting. In July, health minister Preet Kaur Gill repeated the five-trust usage figure in a Parliamentary answer.

Official data released in October said that as of June, six trusts were using Cancer 360 and five were benefiting, but did not identify the trusts or explain the increase. The stats have since been removed from the NHS England website but are archived here.
In June, NHS England responded to a Freedom of Information request. It said six trusts reported unique users logging into the Cancer 360 app over the last 12 months.

However, two trusts cited as having run successful pilots – Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and Royal United Hospitals Bath – were listed as having zero unique users logging into the system during that period, according to NHS England's reply.
Both trusts were said to have received benefits from the system, according to a FoI response sent to campaign group Foxglove in June this year.
The Register asked both trusts and NHS England to explain the discrepancy.

One of the six trusts said to be logging into the cancer app, East Lancashire Hospitals, reported just one unique user. It later confirmed in an FoI response in August that it was not live with the FDP. It had planned to adopt the platform, leading with Cancer 360, but did not have a date for going live with the app.
No Palantir in the NHS also identified trusts that considered Cancer 360 but decided against adopting it.
East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust considered using the app but rejected it because there was "no immediate requirement for it," according to its FoI response.
In its FoI response, Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust said it did not adopt the app because of issues around the metadata requirements.
Meanwhile, official figures on cancer diagnosis waiting times show wider improvements across England. Given Cancer 360's limited uptake, those national gains cannot simply be credited to the app.
In July this year, the UK's statistical regulator told NHS England to ensure ministers are briefed accurately following a row over data used to promote the purported benefits of the Palantir-run FDP.

Campaign group Foxglove had found that nearly a third of NHS trusts using Palantir's health data platform were performing fewer patient procedures than before it went live and that Chelsea and Westminster Hospital accounted for 84 percent of the reported fall in outpatient waiting lists, while only 16 trusts were using the FDP tool. The Office for Statistics Regulation began assessing NHS England's claims about the FDP's performance and the quango included more caveats on its website.

Scrutiny of the FDP's reported benefits comes as the government decides whether to continue the Palantir-led contract beyond February 2027. The initial contract was provided for a term of up to seven years, with a maximum value of £330 million.

Reports this week suggest the government is set to renew the contract, but run a parallel procurement to find an alternative to Palantir as pressure mounts to reduce lock-in to a single vendor and boost sovereign technology.

Palantir was founded with startup money from a CIA-linked VC firm and has relied on close ties with the US intelligence, military, and immigration services since its inception, although its recent growth in the wider business market is notable. ®

a3dbb167ed097c11: SEBERANG JAYA: The Penang Immigration Department crippled a fake immigration e-pass printing syndicate and arrested two Bangladeshi men in Simpang Ampat last night.
State Immigration director Syamsul Fitry Ahmad said the suspects, aged 23 and 32, were detained during a 10pm raid at a rented house following public tip-offs and days of intelligence gathering.
"During the inspection of the premises, we discovered several forged or altered e-pass printouts, including documents bearing the particulars of one of the suspects as well as other foreigners.

"The team also found several foreign passports not belonging to the suspects, alongside a large quantity of altered e-pass printouts believed ready for distribution to buyers," he told reporters at the Penang Immigration headquarters.
Syamsul Fitry said further checks revealed the forged documents were linked to the construction sector, with the syndicate targeting undocumented or overstaying Bangladeshi and Pakistani nationals.
He said the syndicate's modus operandi involved digitally editing details on e-pass and passport copies using a laptop before printing them to deceive authorities and employers.
He said the syndicate was believed to have only started operating recently, adding that it charged between RM50 and RM100 per fake e-pass.
However, he said payment transaction records suggest higher fees may have been collected from some, given that genuine annual renewals start at RM2,000.

"So far, we have detected over 50 suspected forged documents, though the exact number remains under investigation based on evidence recovered at the scene and inside the suspects' laptops and mobile phones," he said.
Enforcement officers also seized mobile phones, laptops and printers used to produce the documents, alongside a car and two motorcycles suspected of being used in the syndicate's operations.
Syamsul Fitry added that while the 23-year-old suspect held a valid passport and construction sector work pass, his accomplice was undocumented.
Investigations are ongoing to determine if the duo are linked to a wider network, he added.

"Physically, the fake e-passes are difficult to detect as they look nearly identical to genuine ones, but immigration officers can verify them through QR code scans and counter system checks," he said.
Both suspects have been remanded for 14 days.

f31604bba4d4f50c: KUALA LUMPUR: Has Malaysian football placed its continental seeding at risk while balancing the demands of domestic clubs and the national team?
This question has come to mind as Harimau Malaya prepare to face China and Yemen in Zhaoqing.

The FA of Malaysia's (FAM) decision to excuse Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) players from the November FIFA window was linked to managing player workloads and protecting Malaysia's AFC Member Association (MA) ranking.
That ranking determines the country's continental club allocations, including its sole direct group-stage slot in the Asian Champions League Elite (ACLE).

Reaching the league stage carries a US$800,000 (RM3.55 million) participation fee from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), making the allocation an important prize for Malaysia's domestic champion.
However, the national team's FIFA ranking also has significant implications, particularly with the preliminary joint 2030 World Cup and 2031 Asian Cup qualifiers draw approaching.
Under FIFA's SUM ranking formula, official friendlies played during designated international windows carry an importance weighting of 10.
For 133rd-ranked Malaysia, a win over 96th-ranked China is worth a projected 6.31 points, while beating 144th-ranked Yemen could add another 4.67 points.
A clean sweep would bring nearly 11 points and potentially lift Malaysia towards 128th in the world.
Meanwhile, two defeats could cost the national team around nine points. The difference between those outcomes represents an estimated 20-point swing, potentially bringing Malaysia down to 139th.
The draw for the World Cup qualifiers will use the November FIFA rankings, with top 26 teams going directly to the second round.
Malaysia, ranked 23rd in Asia, are close to the Pot 1 cut-off, making the China and Yemen results particularly important.
Dropping into Pot 2 could leave Malaysia facing a two-legged knockout tie in the first round.

On paper, Malaysia have not beaten China in 44 years. Their 1-1 draw in Chengdu in Sept 2023 was a creditable result, while their last victories over Yemen were narrow 2-1 wins during the 2015 Asian Cup qualifying campaign.
Interim head coach Tan Cheng Hoe acknowledged the competing considerations between club commitments and national team ambitions.
"Of course, as a coach we have mixed feelings," Cheng Hoe said.

"We need to look after what will be a win-win situation. Definitely, as a coach, we want the best. But at the same time, we need the MA ranking points for JDT. As a coach, I am still doing my job as a national coach. Until now, I leave everything to FAM (FA of Malaysia)."

Cheng Hoe admitted that having the country's best players available would make a difference, particularly with six Selangor players (Harith Haiqal Adam Afkar, Nooa Laine, Ahmad Zikri Khalili, Syahir Bashah and A. Selvan) also withdrawing from the squad due to injuries.
"Definitely, as a coach you want the best players around you because they bring a different quality and a different impact to the team," he said.
"At the same time, we have to give chances to the upcoming young players. We need a bigger pool of players for the national team in the future."

He said candidates and parties should issue their final campaign messages early to avoid breaching election rules.
Fahmi also said voters should cast their ballots early, as rain was expected in several areas.

"For those returning to their hometowns to fulfil their responsibility as voters in Melaka, drive safely, ensure you have enough rest, that your vehicles are well-maintained, and do not drive above the speed limit," he said.
He said the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission would continue monitoring possible offences, including those committed on social media.

Fahmi said the public should rely on verified information from official sources, including the EC's social media platforms and established news organisations, and avoid sharing unverified content from parties with vested interests.
"Please verify, because we find it is not impossible that certain parties may produce content of questionable authenticity. Refer to official sources," he said.
The EC is targeting a voter turnout of 70 per cent in Saturday's election.
The 16th Melaka election will see 79 candidates contesting 28 seats.

4d144b5c74f25022: NIBONG TEBAL: The Prisons Department plans to expand a new family and parenting rehabilitation module nationwide to reduce recidivism rates among inmates.

Prisons Deputy Commissioner-General (Security and Correctional) Rosoman Abu Bakar @ Che Din said the pioneer initiative, Kompas Sejahtera, equipped inmates with essential life skills prior to their reintegration into society.

He said the pilot run involved 30 facilitators from the northern zone correctional institutions — covering Penang, Kedah, Perlis and Perak — and directly benefited 224 male inmates at the Seberang Prai Prison.
"We hope the module owner will allow the Prisons Department to roll out these modules across all correctional institutions in Malaysia," he said at the programme's closing ceremony.
The event was officiated by state Social Development, Welfare and Non-Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Lim Siew Khim.
Kompas Sejahtera was developed through strategic collaborations with Universiti Utara Malaysia and the National Population and Family Development Board.
Rosoman said the department is also working to certify the facilitators' training and is considering submitting the initiative for recognition in the Malaysia Book of Records.

"Inmates who are about to be released must possess the awareness, knowledge and skills to return as responsible fathers, husbands and members of society. This directly reduces the risk of re-offending," he said.
He added that the training modules should also be extended to prison personnel to strengthen their roles as leaders and agents of change within the correctional system.

Addressing the inmates, Rosoman urged them to treat the programme as a turning point, reminding them that a father's responsibility goes beyond material provision to include love, attention, education, guidance and character building.
"Your past is not an obstacle to building a more meaningful future. Opportunities to change are always there, every second, provided you take that first step," he added.
99f8587fbc1c274f: SINGAPORE, Nov 13 — A fifth individual has been charged with money laundering offences in relation to the Nvidia chips case.
Shi Bingzhe, 34, was handed 41 charges today (November 13), for consenting to the commission of fraud by false representation involving the purchase of servers.
This follows earlier charges handed to Jenny Lim, 51; Alan Wei Zhaolun, 49; Aaron Woon Guo Jie, 41; and, Chinese national Li Ming, 51.
Lim, Wei and Woon were charged for fraud and money laundering, while Li was charged with fraud and fraudulent trading.
Meanwhile, four firms — Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, Aperia Cloud Services (II) and Luxuriate Your Life — were charged with false representation.

Shi was the director of Superphi and chief operating officer of NJ Global Financial when the two companies purportedly acquired a total of 917 servers from Aperia International across 41 transactions.
Police said today that Shi had reasonable grounds to believe that those servers represented benefits from Aperia International’s criminal conduct, namely fraud by false representation.
If found guilty of the charges, he could be jailed for up to 10 years, fined up to US$500,000 (RM2.04 million), or both — for each charge.
Following the latest charges today, the total number of individuals charged in court is now five, while six companies, including the two linked to Shi, have also been hauled to court.

The police said they take a serious view of the offences and will not hesitate to take firm action against businesses and individuals who engage in dishonest and criminal practices that contravene Singapore’s laws.
False representations of servers

Singapore launched an independent investigation last year, following an anonymous tip-off about computer servers that might contain Nvidia chips being exported to Malaysia, and possibly to an unknown final destination.

This alert did not come from any country or sovereign entity, but the claim was serious enough for authorities to launch an independent investigation, said Home Affairs Minister K. Shanmugam on March 3, 2025.
In January last year, China’s artificial intelligence (AI) firm DeepSeek launched a free AI tool that wiped out around US$1 trillion off the value of US tech stocks.
That, despite tight restrictions the US had imposed on semiconductor firms in their exports to China.

US lawmakers then singled out Singapore in a letter in January urging the then National Security Adviser Mike Waltz to subject countries to strict licensing requirements if they were not willing to crack down on shipments to China.

In Parliament last February, then Second Minister for Trade and Industry Dr Tan See Leng said that products sold by Nvidia to Singapore that were physically delivered here represented less than one per cent of the chipmaker’s overall revenue.
Dr Tan added the remainder of Nvidia’s revenue billed to business entities in Singapore did not involve physical shipments into the country.
He said Nvidia’s products are mainly deployed here for major enterprises and the Government.

Dr Tan added: “If a company in Singapore is engaged in deceptive or dishonest practices to evade export controls that it is subject to, we will investigate, and we will take the appropriate action in accordance with Singapore laws.
“It is in our national interest to secure access to leading-edge technology and to maintain the integrity of our business environment.”
Later the same month, Wei, Woon and Li were charged.
Megaspeed and Alice Huang

Spotlight on fraud allegedly involving Nvidia chips came under renewed spotlight after Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed’s former managing director Alice Huang’s affair with Nvidia chief executive officer (CEO) Jensen Huang was revealed.
In a statement yesterday night to provide updates on Singapore’s investigations, the Ministry of Home Affairs said Chinese businesswoman Huang, also known as Huang Le, was among those investigated.
She was being investigated for her suspected involvement in the possible offences in Singapore as she was then one of the key controllers of Megaspeed.
“Huang was not based in Singapore, and was not investigated for espionage,” the ministry stated.
As part of the investigations, the Republic sought information relating to Super Micro, a US-based supplier of servers.
This was required to tally information and records in other jurisdictions against the companies’ accounts.

The issue was raised by the police and Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) with US authorities in July last year, and again on several occasions with the US Department of Justice and Federal Bureau of Investigation.
“Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” MHA stated.

Without the information, the police and AGC concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish whether Alice Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated.
However, the police found that she had knowingly provided false information, and was issued with a stern warning and barred from re-entering Singapore.
“Other cases in the past have been dealt with in a similar way,” the ministry noted.
It added that Huang had purportedly provided such inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed.
Her passport was returned to her on February 26 this year, and she left Singapore the same day. — AsiaOne

000930d958bb2657: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Sessions Court here will decide on Jan 20 whether former Perlis Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Azlan Man will be called to enter his defence or acquitted of 10 charges involving alleged false claims and receiving proceeds of illegal activities.
Judge Azura Alwi fixed the date after hearing submissions from the prosecution and defence at the end of the prosecution’s case.
The court also set Feb 10 to 12, March 26, and April 16 and 30, 2027, as trial dates should Azlan be ordered to enter his defence.

Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Noralis Mat submitted that Azlan had made five claims for overseas travel facilities between 2013 and 2017, purportedly in his capacity as Menteri Besar, although investigations found that the trips did not take place on the stated dates.

“The 18th prosecution witness (SP18), former Senior Private Secretary to Azlan, Herwardy Hashim, testified that he was instructed by the accused to provide his bank account number to SP10, former managing director of Sri Kedawang Travel & Tour (W) Sdn Bhd (SKTT), Shafiei Ismail, for the purpose of depositing money received by SKTT into the accused’s account.
“This was because the accused wanted to cancel the trip that had been approved through a local order (LO) and undertake the trip himself,” he said.

Noralis said the testimony of the 17th prosecution witness, former Assistant Accountant at the Management Services Division of the Perlis State Secretary’s Office, Mohd Aswad Abdul Razak, established that claims for overseas holiday travel facilities could not be converted into cash.
He said the allocation was intended to cover overseas travel expenses, while payment to the travel agent had already been confirmed by the Menteri Besar’s Office.

He added that this was supported by the testimony of SP12, Perlis Treasury representative Azmi Abdul Latif, who said Azlan could not receive reimbursement for overseas holiday travel claims that had already been made between 2013 and 2017.
“If the holiday trip is cancelled, the travel agent is responsible for cancelling the local order issued to them,” he said.
Noralis further argued that Azlan’s alleged practice of having the money transferred into his personal account every year could not be dismissed as an innocent mistake.
“If the trip is cancelled, the money should have been returned to the Perlis State Government, not handed over to the accused,” he said.

Meanwhile, defence counsel Burhanudeen Abdul Wahid said the Perlis government allocated annual funds to the Menteri Besar for overseas travel, and the services of a travel agent were required to make the necessary bookings and secure the allocation.
He maintained that the entire claims process had been conducted transparently.
“The prosecution claimed that he did not travel but submitted claims for the trips. However, the investigating officer testified that the accused had travelled on other dates,” he said.
Burhanudeen added that the defence had also submitted passport and immigration records to support its position.

Azlan, 67, is facing five charges of submitting false claims involving overseas holiday travel facilities amounting to more than RM1.18 million, allegedly committed at the Perlis State Secretary’s Office between December 2013 and December 2017.
The claims involved flight ticket quotations to London, United Kingdom, as well as invoices issued by SKTT and Aidil Travel & Tours Sdn Bhd.

He is also facing five charges of receiving proceeds of illegal activities amounting to RM1.06 million between Feb 19, 2014 and December 2017 at several locations, including the Maybank branch in Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, the CIMB Bank branch in Putrajaya and the Sheraton Imperial Hotel here.
In addition, Azlan faces five alternative charges of misappropriating RM1.06 million belonging to the Perlis government, which had been paid to SKTT and Aidil Travel & Tours Sdn Bhd. — Bernama
d421795b05ad012c: PETALING JAYA: Ahli Parlimen Padang Rengas Azahari Hasan bertegas tidak akan menyerahkan kerusinya kepada Barisan Nasional (BN) susulan hasrat Nazri Aziz kembali bertanding di kawasan itu pada PRU16.
Azahari yang kini bersama Wawasan usai dipecat Bersatu pada Februari lalu berkata, beliau akan terus bertanding atas tiket Perikatan Nasional (PN) selepas memenangi kerusi itu pada PRU15.
"Walaupun sekarang Wawasan, kita akan pertahankan kerusi penyandang. Sebab Wawasan di bawah PN, jadi saya akan bertanding balik atas tiket PN.
“Takkan kita mudah-mudah nak serah balik pada BN begitu,” katanya kepada FMT, merujuk kehadiran parti komponen PN seperti PAS dan Gerakan di Padang Rengas.
Bagaimanapun, Azahari berkata hasrat Nazri untuk kembali bertanding sudah berlegar sejak tahun lalu, namun tidak pernah memaklumkan secara peribadi kepadanya.

Terdahulu, Nazri yang mewakili Padang Rengas selama empat penggal dari 2004 hingga 2022 menegaskan kawasan itu kerusi BN dan meminta PN mencari kerusi lain, walaupun gabungan itu kini menjalin kerjasama pilihan raya di beberapa negeri.
Pada PRU15, Azahari menewaskan calon BN Ariff Abdul Majid dengan majoriti 3,046 undi.
Azahari berkata, hampir empat tahun berkhidmat di Padang Rengas tanpa meninggalkan kawasan itu mengukuhkan pendiriannya untuk mempertahankan kerusi berkenaan.
Beliau yang juga ketua Wawasan Padang Rengas berkata, kedudukannya sama seperti Nazri yang masih mengetuai Umno bahagian itu.
“Dia ketua bahagian. Saya pun ketua bahagian Wawasan. Jadi kita pun sama juga kita pun akan pertahankan,” katanya.
Bagaimanapun, beliau menyifatkan hasrat Nazri kembali bertanding sebagai pendirian peribadi, bukannya keputusan rasmi BN.
“Dia punya (hasrat) suara peribadi, bukan mewakili pimpinan tertinggi BN…keputusan akhir parti yang buat,” katanya.
Azahari berkata, belum ada sebarang perbincangan mengenai pertindihan tuntutan kerusi itu dan menyerahkannya kepada pucuk pimpinan kedua-dua gabungan untuk dimuktamad.
“Yang itu kita serah kepada pimpinan atasan. Sebab kalau kita bertemu di bawah ini dia tak boleh buat kata putus," katanya ketika ditanya adakah terdapat rancangan untuk berjumpa Nazri.

Menurutnya, presiden Wawasan sebelum ini tegas mahu mempertahankan 19 kerusi Parlimen miliknya - yang sebelum ini bertanding atas tiket Bersatu - termasuk Padang Rengas, berdasarkan prinsip mengekalkan penyandang.
Namun, beliau tidak menolak kemungkinan pertukaran kerusi menerusi rundingan antara BN dan PN, walaupun berpendapat penyandang sedia ada lebih wajar dikekalkan.
“Ataupun ‘worst to worst’ mungkin ada ‘swaplah’. Walaupun, ‘swap’ tapi ‘better incumbent’ ni kita kekalkan.”
7381b84dd0e3f106: SINGAPORE, Nov 13 — There is no indication that the ongoing Microsoft service outage on Friday (November 13) is the result of malicious or cyber activity, said the company’s executive vice president Charles Lamanna.

“We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity,” the executive wrote.

This, it said, is to improve the ability to confirm the developed changes applied.
“We’re tracking the results of this approach to verify the servers are showing the anticipated recovery and performance intended.”
Millions of companies around the world are estimated to use Microsoft services, including tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic, which have both reported problems as a result of the outage.

1e309a1bafaf8dbb: JOHOR BARU: Despite losing an arm in a 2019 motorcycle crash, a 32-year-old mechanic here can still repair up to five motorcycles a day using only one hand.
Samsul Aripin Sadip, from Kota Tinggi, said many people are amazed by his ability to fix motorcycles with one hand and often assume he was born that way.
He said the crash occurred in 2019 while he was test-riding a customer's motorcycle from Sungai Danga to Puteri Harbour, when the machine skidded and slammed into a road divider.
Severe injuries forced doctors at Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) here to amputate his arm to save his life.
"I was told that if I did not undergo the surgery, I faced risks that could affect my brain nerves.
"I believe in Allah's plan, and I accepted my fate at the time because I was thinking about my future and did not want to burden my parents.
"My parents were also my source of strength. Although they were initially distressed by what happened, I rested for a few months before retraining myself to repair motorcycles using my left hand.

"It was certainly a challenge because it felt awkward working with my left hand after being used to my right, but with continuous practice, my confidence grew," said Samsul Aripin, who now lives at Flat Sri Lanang in Tebrau.
He said he was grateful to receive job offers from several motorcycle workshops and has been working at a workshop in Jalan Harmonium 23/14, Taman Desa Tebrau here for the past year.
He is able to repair between two and five motorcycles daily, depending on whether the damage involves the engine or only external parts.
"I have had a passion for fixing motorcycles since I was 14, when I was in Form Two, and it allowed me to earn a side income as a teenager.
"No matter the damage, including on high-powered motorcycles, I try my best to fix it without giving up, and if it takes too long, I ask my colleagues for help.
"I work from noon to 11pm, and I am grateful that customers are satisfied with my work."
Samsul Aripin added that he hopes to deepen his skills in the field and inspire others facing similar adversity.
