1b9340bce4797556: TEHRAN, Nov 13 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said today that a ship was hit by an explosion after striking a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, where Tehran has sought to restrict navigation.
Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has insisted that vessels obtain its authorisation to traverse the strait and has attacked vessels that do not comply.
The US has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and provides military support to tankers using the vital trade route.

“A few hours ago, a ship carrying liquefied natural gas east of the Strait of Hormuz tried to cross an unauthorised passageway south of the strait, but was hit by a naval mine and exploded violently,” the Guards said today.
They did not give the name or origin of the vessel.
In recent weeks, Iran’s armed forces have repeatedly reported fires or explosions on board ships in the strait, often saying the vessels struck mines.
The US military, however, claims to have cleared the main routes through the waterway of mines.

The Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, also said overnight that their forces had targeted a US early warning radar system in Bahrain, a US ally in the Gulf that is home to American military installations.
The attack was not confirmed by either the US or Bahrain. — AFP
bea7e0ae573bcfe1: THE HAGUE: Dutch prime minister Rob Jetten was to hold crisis talks with key partners Friday in a last-ditch bid to save his minority coalition government from collapse only nine months after taking power.
An unseemly political row over tax policy has raised the spectre of snap elections in the EU's fifth-largest economy and weakened the centrist Jetten, the country's youngest-ever prime minister.
Since winning a razor-thin election, Jetten's D66 party has been in an uneasy three-way coalition with the centre-right CDA and the right-wing VVD.
After months of complex debate over tax policy, the D66 and CDA struck a deal with the opposition left-wing PRO party, enraging the VVD.
VVD leader Dilan Yesilgoz, also defence minister, lashed out, saying the coalition would require a "fundamental reset" if her partners sided with the opposition.
"We have been blindsided by a proposal that, in our view, jeopardises the stability of the Netherlands, our economic growth and our business climate," fumed Yesilgoz.
Following a whole day of debate Thursday, the tax deal won a razor-thin parliamentry majority but the VVD voted against the government's own policy, shattering the whole foundation of the coalition.
The PM himself acknowledged there would need to be a "serious fresh start" and called in Yesilgoz and a top CDA official for showdown talks Friday morning.

Jetten, 39, is hamstrung politically as his coalition has only 66 seats in the 150-member parliament, meaning he needs to cobble together votes from smaller parties -- or the opposition -- to pass legislation.
No fewer than 15 parties hold seats in the Dutch parliament, from those defending the interests of people over 50 years old, to a farmers' party.
This means any legislation is the result of many months of squabbling and compromise.
An election would be the third in three years for the splintered country, a key member of the Nato military alliance that also punches above its weight in the EU.
The latest polls show PRO and its youthful leader Jesse Klaver would win any election, ahead of the far-right PVV led by firebrand Geert Wilders.

"This coalition is effectively dead. We just have to wait for the funeral to take place," said Wilders, who sparked elections in 2025 when he pulled his party out of government in a row over immigration.
a30f9de2b4e8063b: SINGAPORE, Nov 13 — Microsoft services have been hit with an outage since Thursday (November 12), resulting in many users across Singapore affected, particularly as they attempt to access email for work.
Randy Tan, a research analyst who uses his email to keep track of current affairs, told AsiaOne on Friday (November 13) that access to Outlook has been impacted.
While he said that his workflow hasn’t been affected that much as of yet, Tan expressed concern about what comes after the outage is resolved.
“I worry that the longer the delay, the larger the backlog of emails to look into and thus having to make more time later on to clear them,” he said.
Human resources manager Priscilla Lim was hit harder by the outage as her work relies heavily on email.
Not only has the disruption affected her ability to respond to ongoing situations, she also has to reroute communications to other platforms to keep work moving, she explained.
“It’s definitely inconvenient and frustrating, especially when email is such an integral part of our daily operations.”
Researcher Grace Ow said the situation was frustrating.
“While we do have some workarounds, it makes day-to-day tasks less efficient,” she said.
Online, many users in Singapore also shared their views on the outage, with some concerned over complications that this may bring.
“As someone working in IT, (I’m mentally exhausted) and don’t know what to expect when I come to work later,” a user on Reddit said.
Another bemoaned: “You mean we have to do our meetings face to face today?”
But others saw this as an opportunity to appreciate a slower Friday.
“Ah no wonder,” commented one. “I keep refreshing my Outlook but it’s not working, means it’s time to pang kang (go home) early.”
Joked another: “Take your own time, Microsoft IT guys, no job is worth sacrificing your peace and mental health. Come back and fix it next Monday when you are fresh and rested.”
According to outage tracker Downdetector, the number of outage reports in Singapore peaked at 567 at around 9.30am and has been declining since.
Microsoft acknowledged the outage at around 2.30am on Friday, where they stated that some Microsoft 365 services have been experiencing “elevated load” in multiple regions.
This prompted them to begin maintenance and repair operations, as well as review the situation and evaluate their options to redirect traffic to other infrastructure.
Since then, Microsoft has restarted the affected infrastructure after noting that a process on the impacted servers had been overwhelmed, causing the servers to stop processing requests.
They have seen positive results since then and began applying infrastructure capacity improvements to help support traffic in regions coming online, such as Singapore.
However, access to email is still limited as change is “not taking as expected”, Microsoft stated in an update just before 11am. — AsiaOne
85d1b9ab9e07655d: SYDNEY, Nov 13 — Cases of Indigenous women shackled while giving birth and growing numbers of children in detention are “embarrassing” to Australia, the UN’s special rapporteur on Indigenous rights said today.

UN Special Rapporteur Albert Barume said he visited Australia because he saw Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s attempt to recognise First Nations people in the constitution as a sign of progress, despite a national referendum failing to pass in 2023.

Barume ended his two-week visit today with a bleak message that Indigenous people’s rights are “unsafe” in Australia because they are controlled by states and territories, not the national government.
“The state of protection of Indigenous people’s rights is a bit embarrassing. I heard the story of women giving birth shackled — I couldn’t believe it,” he told a news conference in Sydney.
Rights groups say the practice used for some women prisoners disproportionately impacts Indigenous women who experience higher rates of incarceration.
An Indigenous lawmaker sought to introduce a bill to stop the practice in the federal parliament in August.

Australia’s international reputation was at stake, Barume said, after he was denied access to youth detention centres in Queensland state and the Northern Territory, which have the highest rates of Indigenous youth incarceration.
Officials in these states also refused to meet him.
“If you cannot be subjected to international scrutiny, you should not be in charge of human rights,” he said.
The national government should be “the sole and only duty bearer for human rights”, he added.
Over 90 per cent of children in detention in Queensland and the Northern Territory are Indigenous, government data shows.
Indigenous Australians make up 6.6 per cent of the youth population, but 60 per cent of children aged 10 to 17 in detention nationally.
Among incarcerated children aged 10 to 13 years, 79 per cent are Indigenous.
Barume said Australia should establish a national minimum age of criminal responsibility of 14 years and invest in programmes to prevent crime instead of jailing “huge numbers” of children.
“First Peoples’ children require culturally appropriate care, protection, education, family and community support — not criminalisation,” he said.
The failure of a national referendum on Indigenous recognition three years ago had “opened a floodgate of racism”, he said, urging Albanese’s government “not to abandon the idea”.
The Australian attorney-general’s office said the decision by Queensland and the Northern Territory not to cooperate with UN envoy’s visit “does not reflect the position of the Albanese government”.
It said it was working with the states to implement Australia’s international obligations. — AFP
abbb209dd29b7a22: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the "political temperature" in the Cabinet remains under control despite tensions arising from remarks made by several leaders in the unity government.
Anwar said the political climate usually heats up slightly during elections, but returns to normal once the polls are over.
He said today’s Cabinet meeting proceeded as usual with both deputy prime ministers and other ministers present, and discussions focused on development and other matters.

“When there is an election, the temperature rises briefly. Then it comes down again. But today’s (Cabinet) meeting was normal. I did not detect any problems,” he told reporters after Friday prayers in Brickfields here.
He was asked about the Cabinet meeting amid political tensions during the Melaka state election campaign.
Yesterday, deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi reaffirmed his support for Anwar, saying there was no reason for any Barisan Nasional minister to resign from the Cabinet.

Instead, the BN chairman said, DAP ministers should follow the example of party secretary-general Loke Siew Fook, who resigned as transport minister on Tuesday over the issue of former prime minister Najib Razak's house arrest.
Zahid was responding to DAP chairman and digital minister Gobind Singh Deo, who suggested that he resign as deputy prime minister if he no longer had confidence in Anwar’s leadership.
On Tuesday, Zahid said dissolving Parliament would be preferable to a Cabinet reshuffle.
He said he saw no need for changes to the Cabinet, and that a fresh mandate should be sought from the people before a new government was formed.
His remarks came amid speculation of a Cabinet reshuffle following the end of finance minister II Amir Hamzah Azizan’s term as a senator on Dec 11, and Loke’s resignation.
Anwar said Loke was the only minister absent from today’s Cabinet meeting, and that he needed more time to consider his resignation.
“I have not accepted his resignation. I have received the letter, and he said it would take effect (from Tuesday) but I will need time to review it.
“There is no need for us to rush,” he said.
3893711e811b7eea: KUALA LUMPUR: Tiada sebarang petunjuk cip kecerdasan buatan (AI) yang dikaitkan dengan isu Nvidia-Megaspeed dieksport dari Malaysia, kata Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.
“Tiada sebarang petunjuk tentang perkara itu (setakat ini),” katanya kepada pemberita apabila ditanya mengenai perkara itu.
Anwar turut berkata, Menteri Pelaburan, Perdagangan dan Industri Johari Abdul Ghani telah memberikan laporan mengenai perkara itu pagi ini.
"Kami akan bekerjasama dengan semua agensi yang terlibat,” katanya ketika ditemui selepas menunaikan solat Jumaat di Madrasathul Gouthiyyah, di Brickfields.

Mengenai sama ada Malaysia telah menerima permintaan rasmi daripada Singapura atau Amerika Syarikat (AS) berhubung siasatan terhadap isu Nvidia-Megaspeed, Anwar berkata, setakat ini negara belum menerima sebarang permohonan daripada kedua-dua negara tersebut.
“Buat masa ini, kita belum menerima sebarang permintaan sedemikian. Namun, sudah tentu kita akan bekerjasama.
“Kita negara perdagangan. Kita mengalu-alukan pelaburan. Kita mahu memastikan peraturan dipatuhi,” katanya.

Terdahulu hari ini, Kementerian Pelaburan, Perdagangan dan Industri (Miti) memaklumkan tidak pernah memberikan kelulusan kepada Megaspeed International Pte Ltd yang berpangkalan di Singapura atau syarikat sekutunya di Malaysia, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd.
Menurut Miti, Speedmatrix ialah penyewa pusat data di Malaysia dan membawa masuk pelayan dan cip AI milik sendiri ke negara ini untuk tujuan operasinya.

Dalam kenyataan, kementerian itu memaklumkan sedang bekerjasama dengan Jabatan Kastam untuk menentukan sama ada mana-mana cip tersebut telah dieksport semula ke negara lain atau mematuhi undang-undang Malaysia.
Menurut Miti, kemasukan cip AI ke Malaysia pada masa ini tidak memerlukan sebarang permit atau lesen.

Bagaimanapun, mulai Julai 2025, mana-mana pihak yang ingin mengeksport, mengeksport semula, memindah cip AI berprestasi tinggi AS dari atau melalui Malaysia, perlu terlebih dahulu mendapatkan permit daripada Miti di bawah Akta Perdagangan Strategik 2010.
“Memberikan maklumat palsu kepada pihak Kastam mengenai barangan sedemikian juga merupakan satu kesalahan serius di bawah Akta Kastam 1967,” menurut kementerian.
Miti memaklumkan, Malaysia akan menjalankan pemeriksaannya sendiri selaras dengan undang-undang negara dan berdasarkan bukti yang ada.
4d5cf4154b323cad: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Queen of Rock, Ella, will wrap up her Majlis Tertinggi concert series with a grand finale, Majlis Tertinggi Rockqueen Ella: Sidang Penutup, at Unifi Arena, Bukit Jalil, on Dec 5.
Hitman Group CEO Rohit Rampal revealed the concert was planned at the last minute after Ella expressed her wish to host a closing show.
"Actually, this 'closing' was 'hijacked' the other day. Recently, Kak El (Ella) told us about her desire to hold a closing concert for Majlis Tertinggi Rockqueen," he said.
"We will be sharing the date with an international concert, but we will do our utmost to deliver an extraordinary experience. This is the best way to end the year with our Queen of Rock."
Despite competing local and international concerts on the same date, Rohit remains confident about ticket sales.
"Whenever Kak El wants to do a concert, I don't worry about the crowd or ticket sales. That is never our concern," he said.
"We already have a 300,000-strong fan community via email and WhatsApp. Maintaining good ties with fans is vital, and we know tickets will sell fast."
Rockqueen brand director Captain Azhar also described the upcoming show as a gift of appreciation for the loyal fans who have supported Ella.
Ella, whose real name is Nor Zila Aminuddin, 60, said she decided to invite Yuna and Datuk Ziana Zain as guest artistes to offer something fresh on stage.
"I chose Yuna and Datuk Ziana Zain because I wanted something different on stage," said Ella, adding that her admiration for their talent and their close friendship were key factors.
"I even attended Yuna's wedding, and we are practically neighbours. Why not bring them up on stage with me?"
Jointly organised by Hitman Solutions and Rockqueen, Sidang Penutup will feature a meet-and-greet session and a fan-chosen setlist.
Hitman Solutions head of special projects Keeran D noted that Unifi Arena was picked following fan requests for a comfortable, air-conditioned venue.
The Majlis Tertinggi Rockqueen tour kicked off earlier this year with 55,000 fans at the TM National Stadium in Bukit Jalil, followed by over 5,000 fans in Singapore and 10,000 in Penang.
Attracting more than 70,000 concertgoers across three shows, the tour highlights Ella's lasting legacy and ability to unite fans after four decades in music.
Ella hopes the finale, designed as a night of celebration, will be unforgettable.

"This year has been an 'extraordinary' and meaningful journey for me. From fans at the National Stadium Bukit Jalil to Singapore and Penang, I am deeply grateful to have the opportunity to share music with so many supportive fans," she said.

"Every journey must have an end, and every story has its final chapter. I want Sidang Penutup to be a truly special night for all of us – closing this year's Majlis Tertinggi Rockqueen journey with joy, love and memories we will cherish forever. Since we started together, let us bring the curtain down together as well."
009a5e3a83dfcff1: MELAKA: Keputusan membenarkan bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak menjalani tahanan rumah mengundang reaksi berbeza dalam kalangan pengundi Melaka, namun isu itu tidak semestinya menjadi penentu pilihan mereka pada PRN esok.
Sebaliknya, sebahagian pengundi lebih mahu melihat parti politik menawarkan penyelesaian terhadap masalah rakyat, termasuk gangguan bekalan air dan kesesakan lalu lintas.

Tinjauan FMT mendapati, ada yang menyokong keputusan itu kerana mengenang jasa Najib ketika menerajui negara, manakala yang lain berpendapat beliau sepatutnya kekal menjalani hukuman di Penjara Kajang.
Pesara kerajaan, Rosna Mohamad Yusuf, 67, antara yang menyokong keputusan itu kerana menghargai sumbangan Najib, khususnya terhadap kebajikan penjawat awam.

“Bagi saya, selayaknyalah dia diberi kelonggaran itu. Kami orang lama ini tahu banyak jasa dia. Tambahan pula saya bekas kakitangan kerajaan di bawah Kementerian Kewangan, banyak perkara yang dia berikan kepada kami,” katanya.
Semalam, Timbalan Presiden PAS, Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, berkata isu tahanan rumah Najib memberi momentum kepada Umno pada PRN Melaka dan mampu berterusan hingga PRU akan datang.
Najib mula menjalani baki hukuman penjara enam tahun dalam kes SRC International Sdn Bhd menerusi tahanan rumah pada Selasa lalu. Hukuman itu dijadual tamat pada 23 Ogos 2028.
Umno menubuhkan tabung untuk mengumpul dana bagi membayar denda RM50 juta dikenakan terhadap Najib dalam kes itu yang membolehkannya menjalani tahanan rumah berkenaan.
Setiausaha Agung DAP, Loke Siew Fook, pula menggesa pengundi di Melaka yang tidak berpuas hati dengan perkembangan itu menyuarakan pandangan mereka melalui peti undi, esok.
M Subramaniam, 59, dari Jasin, pula berkata Najib banyak membantu masyarakat India tanpa mengabaikan kaum dan agama lain sepanjang pentadbirannya.
“Dia macam ayah saya. Saya memang tidak lupa jasa-jasanya,” katanya yang lebih berharap Najib dibebaskan sepenuhnya.

Bagi Safiyah Sudin, 70, keputusan berhubung tahanan rumah itu perlu dihormati kerana melibatkan kuasa pengampunan Yang di-Pertuan Agong, selain mengambil kira sumbangan Najib terhadap pembangunan negara.
Wong Aik, 42, turut menggesa semua pihak menghormati keputusan itu dan tidak menjadikan isu Najib sebagai modal kempen pilihan raya sehingga menyebabkan rakyat muak dengan politik.
“Lagipun Najib bukan bebas lagi, cuma tempat tahanan sahaja berubah. Daripada main isu Najib, lebih baik cerita apa nak ditawarkan kepada rakyat.
“Rakyat akan lihat mana pihak beri tawaran terbaik untuk memberi undi, bukan nak dengar isu Najib sahaja,” katanya.
Bagaimanapun, Ravindran, 60, pula berpandangan Najib sepatutnya kekal di penjara selepas didapati bersalah dan dijatuhi hukuman.

“Dia didapati bersalah dan sudah dihukum masuk penjara. Patutnya duduk penjara. Di penjara pun saya rasa dia sudah mendapat layanan istimewa, jadi kalau benarkan dia duduk di rumah, nanti jadi isu juga,” katanya.

Pandangan itu dikongsi Jan Lim, 54, yang mahu Najib terus menjalani hukuman di Penjara Kajang, manakala Mat Tahir Ahamad, 66, mempersoalkan kos dan penggunaan sumber bagi menyediakan kawalan keselamatan di kediaman bekas perdana menteri itu, selain bimbang kesannya terhadap imej negara.
Walaupun membantah tahanan rumah Najib, Ravindran menegaskan isu itu bukan keutamaan dalam menentukan undinya pada PRN Melaka.
Sebaliknya, beliau mahu memilih wakil rakyat yang mampu menyelesaikan masalah penduduk, khususnya gangguan bekalan air dan kesesakan lalu lintas.
“Saya nak pemimpin yang boleh bersuara untuk rakyat dan melayan kehendak mereka. Bukannya muncul lima tahun sekali, masa nak mengundi sahaja,” katanya.
72a5a35ef94eff47: BEIJING, Nov 13 — China warned the US today against putting additional export controls on semiconductors in the wake of the scandal surrounding AI chip giant Nvidia.

China “has consistently opposed the abuse of export control measures, which disrupts the stability of global industrial and supply chains and serves no party’s interests,” foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular briefing when asked about calls from US lawmakers to impose more limits on exports of chip equipment to China.

“China and the US should work together to implement the important consensus reached by their respective heads of state and maintain the stable development of China-US economic and trade relations,” Mao said.
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang — who resigned yesterday — has admitted to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.
Reports allege the Commerce Department under Secretary Howard Lutnick may have failed to act on suspicions that Megaspeed was helping reroute restricted Nvidia technology to China.
US media quoted US lawmakers as saying that they were in favour of imposing additional export controls on chips to China as a result of the snowballing scandal.
“The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here. I’m in favour of limiting those exports,” House speaker Mike Johnson was quoted as saying.
“I think there is a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take.”
US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging that Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen Huang — was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
Beijing has rejected the allegations and yesterday said that they are a “pretext to for imposing a technological blockade” to stop China advancing in artificial intelligence technology.
The furore comes ahead of a meeting expected next week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Shenzhen in southern China at a APEC gathering. — AFP
0fca2013c0d0c9b9: KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor needs to speed up drain and river cleaning to reduce flooding, following Kuala Lumpur's example, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
"The menteri besar (Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari) has approved additional funding and action at all levels. But we feel there is a need to move faster, as Kuala Lumpur does.
"In Kuala Lumpur, drains and rivers are cleaned six times a year instead of twice, helping to reduce flooding," he said.
Anwar was speaking to reporters after performing Friday prayers at Madrasathul Gouthiyyah Surau in Brickfields.
He said the menteri besar had provided additional funds, while district and municipal councils had been instructed to ensure drains and waterways were cleaned.
"Starting today, there must be no delays. We are taking action to the best of our ability," he said.
As of 8am today, the number of flood victims at relief centres had increased in Selangor but decreased in Perak.
In Selangor, the number of flood victims at seven relief centres rose to 1,248 from 1,144, while the number of families increased to 338 from 318 yesterday.
Selangor has been hit by repeated flash floods in recent weeks, with Kampung Melayu Subang among the worst-affected areas.
Nearly 550 homes and about 1,500 residents in the village were affected by four floods, with damage reported to homes, vehicles and belongings.
34aedc2a0fa6cb6c: KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities seized 64,100 litres of suspected misappropriated diesel worth RM439,085 and arrested four people, including a foreigner, during a raid at an industrial premises in Kedah on Wednesday.

The 11.30pm raid was carried out by Bukit Aman's Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) under the Internal Security and Public Order Department, in collaboration with Kedah Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry enforcement officers.
WCB/PSK commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said those detained were believed to have acted as lorry drivers, workers and the premises owner.
He said further checks at the site led to the seizure of equipment and vehicles believed to have been used in the diesel misappropriation activity.

"The seizures involved two tanker lorries containing about 4,500 litres and 14,000 litres of diesel respectively, as well as three skid tanks containing about 18,000 litres, 13,000 litres and 14,000 litres of the fuel.

"Also seized were an intermediate bulk container (IBC) tank holding about 600 litres of diesel, two oil suction pumps, two metered suction pumps, three mobile phones, as well as equipment and vehicle keys believed to be linked to the activity," he said in a statement today.
Zaki said the total value of the seizures, including related components, was estimated at RM1,074,585.

All suspects, together with the seized vehicles, diesel and equipment, were handed over to the Kedah Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Kuala Muda police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department for further action and investigation.
"Investigations are also focusing on the involvement of each suspect and identifying whether there are other networks or parties linked to the misappropriation," he said.

He said the case is being investigated under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961 and Section 55B of the Immigration Act 1959/63, adding that enforcement will be intensified through intelligence, monitoring and integrated operations to curb the misappropriation and abuse of controlled goods.
b05f86032470fe6c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today described the mood at this morning’s Cabinet meeting as “normal”, amid signs of disunity within the government as his Pakatan Harapan coalition goes head-to-head with its unity government ally, Barisan Nasional, in tomorrow’s Melaka state polls.
Anwar played down the tension in the run-up to tomorrow’s vote as part and parcel of an election campaign, and said he anticipates the temperature to cool down again once the election is done.

“When there is an election, the temperature rises briefly. Then it goes back down. But as for the meeting earlier, it was normal. I didn’t notice any issues,” Anwar told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Brickfields here.

Media reports suggested there is growing friction within Anwar’s Cabinet, as the two major governing coalitions traded salvos at the Melaka election campaign trail where incumbent BN had teamed up with rivals Perikatan Nasional to defend the state.

One of Anwar’s staunchest backers, Anthony Loke, has also resigned as transport minister in what is seen as a protest against the conditional royal clemency granted to Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Razak, allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his jail sentence for his SRC International corruption convictions at home.
Anwar said he has yet to decide whether to accept Loke’s resignation and was in no rush to do so.
“I have not accepted the resignation yet. I have received the letter and he said it takes effect (immediately), but I will certainly take some time to review it carefully,” he told reporters.
“There is no need for us to rush.”
bf6fd87eeb58db57: PUTRAJAYA: Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) holders who meet the minimum entry requirement of B4 in five stipulated subjects will remain eligible to apply for direct entry into medical degree programmes at private universities.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the cabinet had decided to retain the entry requirements that were in place before the recent amendment to the Education Act.

"Therefore, UEC holders who meet the minimum requirement of B4 in the five stipulated subjects remain eligible to apply for direct entry into medical degree programmes at private higher education institutions (IPTS)," he said at his weekly post-cabinet meeting press conference.

Under the amendment, the UEC, administered by the United Chinese School Committees' Association of Malaysia (Dong Zong) for Chinese independent secondary schools, is not recognised by the federal government as an entry qualification for public universities.

Fahmi said the Health Ministry and Malaysian Medical Council (MMC) would coordinate follow-up action with the Higher Education Ministry to ensure the admission process ran smoothly and address any issues that might arise.
He said the move would also ensure that the standards and quality of medical education in the country, including at private institutions, remained protected.
B4 is equivalent to a credit grade under the UEC grading system.
Under existing MMC guidelines, UEC qualifications are recognised for admission into medical programmes at private higher education institutions only.
b0bb0a2bd6a1f921: KUALA LUMPUR: Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King will look to avenge their compatriots' defeats against Denmark's Daniel Lundgaard-Mads Vestergaard in Saturday's Kumamoto Masters men's doubles semi-finals in Japan.
A victory for the world No. 57 will also keep compatriots Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik's World Tour Finals qualification hopes alive.
Aaron Tai-Roy King reached the semi-finals after upsetting Taiwan's world No. 15 Lee Jhe Huei-Yang Po Hsuan 21-16, 21-12 in 28 minutes at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium on Friday.
It was their second straight upset in the tournament after defeating world No. 5 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin 21-14, 21-15 in the second round a day earlier.

World No. 14 Lundgaard-Vestergaard overcame Japan's Hiroki Okamura-Kyohei Yamashita 21-14, 21-14 in their quarter-final match, having beaten Malaysia's Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub-Tan Wee Kiong and Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun in the opening two rounds.
National coach Chang Kim Wai urged Tai-Roy King to maintain consistency against the Danes.
"The Danish pair are currently on form, but so are Aaron Tai-Roy King," said Kim Wai.
"There is still a chance for Aaron Tai-Roy King to reach the final. I believe the pair that maintains focus and perform will win the semi-final encounter."
Lundgaard-Vestergaard sit just 130 points behind Aaron Chia-Wooi Yik, who currently occupy the eighth and final qualifying spot for the season-ending World Tour Finals in Hangzhou next month.

Aaron Chia-Wooi Yik remain in contention for one of the eight men's doubles berths despite injury concerns disrupting their campaign, with the latter recovering from a heel problem and the former troubled by a shoulder issue.

With the Danes close behind in the Race to Finals standings, another victory for Lundgaard-Vestergaard would strengthen their bid for a place in Hangzhou, whereas an Aaron Tai-Roy King win would prevent them from collecting more points.
For Aaron Tai-Roy King, the semi-final also offers an opportunity to extend their strong start as partners.
The pair have reached three semi-finals in five tournaments since joining forces last month, winning the Arctic Open on debut before making the last four at the Hylo Open in Germany.
Another victory would put them through to their second final together and keep alive their hopes of adding another World Tour title to their collection.
47b0a432772b9718: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has dismissed the government's appeal against a ruling declaring a 37-year-old woman, who was abandoned shortly after birth, a Malaysian citizen by operation of law.
A three-member panel chaired by Justice Firuz Jaffril, sitting with Justices Ismail Ibrahim and Dean Wayne Daly, also ordered the government to pay the woman RM10,000 in costs.

In its judgment, the court upheld a High Court finding that the woman qualified for citizenship under Article 14(1)(b), read together with Section 1(a) of Part II and Section 19B of Part III of the Second Schedule to the Federal Constitution.
Section 19B provides that a newborn child found exposed in any place is presumed, unless the contrary is established, to have been born there to a mother permanently resident at that place.
Firuz said Section 19B must be interpreted broadly to protect newborn children abandoned by mothers whose identities are unknown.

“The broadest possible interpretation of the word ‘found exposed’ is to accord it a meaning to include a child abandoned at the place of birth by the birth mother whose identity is unknown,” he said in the 27-page judgment delivered today.

Firuz said the government had failed to produce sufficient evidence to rebut the statutory presumption, adding that the mere fact that the biological parents were unidentified was insufficient to do so.

The woman was found abandoned shortly after birth in May 1989 in Kepong, Kuala Lumpur, and was subsequently raised by adoptive parents. An adoption order was granted by the Ipoh sessions court in 2009.
However, the national registration department maintained her citizenship status as undetermined before issuing her a temporary identity card bearing the status “bukan warganegara” (not a citizen).

The Court of Appeal clarified that adoption by Malaysian citizens did not confer citizenship by itself, but the woman's entitlement arose from the constitutional presumption applicable to abandoned newborns.
The panel relied on the 2022 Federal Court's decision in CCH & Anor v Pendaftar Besar Kelahiran dan Kematian Malaysia, which established the approach to interpreting Section 19B.

“We find no error in the High Court judge’s overall decision warranting appellate intervention. The judge had correctly appreciated the evidence and applied the principles laid down by the Federal Court in CCH,” said Firuz.
Although costs are generally not awarded in public interest cases, Firuz said the respondent's lawyers had undertaken research and preparation in responding to the appeal.
Senior federal counsel Norazlinawati Arshad and federal counsel Jicent Yee appeared for the government. C Shanmugamoorthy, M Yogamani, M Praveena, M Shahgambahri and R Yashemi represented the woman.
5f7b14ff37d005c9: SINGAPORE: Singapore charged a fifth person in a fraud case linked to the export of computer hardware suspected of containing Nvidia chips subject to US trade restrictions.
Shi Bingzhe, 34, was handed 41 charges, including for money laundering offences, on Friday, Singapore police said in a statement.
Police also handed separate charges to Superphi Pte and NJ Global Financial Pte, two companies where Shi worked as a director.
Authorities in Singapore and elsewhere in Southeast Asia are stepping up their scrutiny of shipments of advanced Nvidia AI chips that the US suspects are being smuggled to China via the region.

Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Thursday after revelations that he had a relationship with Alice Huang, a former CEO of a Singapore-based firm also suspected of helping Chinese companies procure Nvidia chips.
With Shi’s consent, Singaporean firms Superphi and NJ Global acquired a total of 917 servers from Aperia International Pte across 41 transactions between May 2024 and February 2025, police said.
The firms had reasonable grounds to believe that those servers represented benefits from Aperia International’s criminal conduct including fraud by false representation, they said.

If convicted, Shi faces up to 10 years in jail for each case, or a fine of up to S$500,000, or both. Superphi and NJ Global face a fine of up to S$1 million or twice the value of the benefits from criminal conduct, whichever is higher, for each charge.
Four companies connected to the case were charged in July with fraud by false representation: Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech Pte, Aperia Cloud Services (II) Pte and Luxuriate Your Life Pte.
Police said then the case involved alleged false statements about the end-users of servers bought from Dell Technologies Inc, Super Micro Computer Inc, and Asustek Computer Inc.

Apart from Shi, Singapore has charged four others with related offences, including fraud, money laundering and fraudulent trading. Prosecutors said in March 2025 the alleged transactions totalled about US$390 million.
The case has put Singapore and Malaysia under scrutiny over whether advanced AI hardware subject to US export curbs was being routed through the region.

Singapore launched an independent investigation after an anonymous tip and has said it is examining potential breaches of domestic law. Malaysia separately investigated whether local laws were breached by the server shipments.
Singapore said last year the servers were shipped onward to Malaysia and may have contained Nvidia chips.
Authorities have been trying to determine whether Malaysia was the final destination in the case, which has highlighted the role of middlemen in funneling high-end semiconductors.
d191e19144474b20: SEREMBAN, Nov 13 — A total of 261 police officers and personnel from Negeri Sembilan have been deployed to help ensure smooth and orderly polling in the 16th Melaka State Election tomorrow.
Negeri Sembilan Police Chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the deployment began yesterday to facilitate early preparations for polling.
“Logistical arrangements and personnel movements in Melaka will be subject to the directives and operational requirements there.
“We will extend the necessary cooperation to help ensure public safety and order throughout the election process,” he told Bernama here today.
The Election Commission (EC) said 675,166 ordinary voters are eligible to cast their ballots tomorrow, with turnout expected to reach 70 per cent. — Bernama
c2c3846c0510529e: SINGAPORE, Nov 13 — A woman who recorded four-year-old Megan Khung’s abuse and helped dispose of her body was sentenced to 13 years’ jail today, with the High Court rejecting suggestions that she was merely a bystander.
CNA reported that Justice S Mohan found Nouvelle Chua Ruoshi, 36, had enabled and participated in the abuse through her filming, continued presence and failure to intervene.
The judge said Megan had endured “wanton acts of cruelty” and that sentences must reflect society’s abhorrence of harm inflicted on vulnerable children.

Chua had pleaded guilty to an amalgamated charge of conspiring to commit child abuse, a charge of disposing of a corpse and another of drug consumption, with three further counts of conspiring to ill-treat Megan taken into consideration.

She was a friend of Megan’s mother, Foo Li Ping, 31, and Foo’s boyfriend, Wong Shi Xiang, 40, who were sentenced in April 2025 to 19 years’ jail and 30 years’ jail with 17 strokes of the cane respectively.
According to CNA’s account of Chua’s earlier plea hearing, she filmed several instances of abuse and dressed Megan in clothing that concealed her bruises and cane marks.
Despite seeing the child weaken as the abuse escalated, Chua did not seek help for her.
After Wong punched Megan in the stomach on February 21, 2020, Chua arrived at the flat after midnight and found the girl lying on the bedroom floor in pain.

CNA reported that Chua alerted the couple to Megan’s complaint but, after they dismissed it as attention-seeking, took drugs with them instead, before the child was found unresponsive several hours later.
At today’s sentencing, Justice Mohan acknowledged Chua’s stated wish to change and encouraged her to reflect on her actions during her imprisonment.
Separately, Singapore’s Ministry of Social and Family Development acknowledged in November 2025 that agencies had missed opportunities to detect Megan’s abuse which might have prevented her death.
292301961dc8afbd: PETALING JAYA: Pakatan Harapan secretary-general Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has criticised PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang for claiming at a ceramah last night that even the worst Muslim rulers are less oppressive than non-Muslims.
Saifuddin said such remarks were regrettable as they judged leaders based on religion rather than their character, integrity, actions and sense of responsibility.
He said Islam teaches its followers to uphold justice, even towards those they dislike.
“It is deeply regrettable that some have concluded that an oppressive Muslim is still better than a non-Muslim simply because of their religious differences.
“A leader should not be judged solely by their religious identity, but by their trustworthiness, commitment to justice and ability to protect the people," he said in a statement.

Saifuddin cautioned against using religion to provide moral protection for corrupt leaders, saying that Islam’s nobility came from justice, good character, knowledge, integrity and exemplary leadership.
He said the strength of the Malays and Muslims would not be diminished by respecting the rights of other races and religions.
“On the contrary, Muslims will earn greater respect when they set the best example in justice, progress, wisdom and compassion towards all humanity,” he said.

Saifuddin said elections should allow voters to assess candidates and parties based on their track record, integrity and capabilities, rather than become a platform for stirring racial and religious fear and prejudice.
His remarks came after Hadi told a BN-PN campaign rally in Bukit Katil, Melaka, last night that “even the most wicked Muslim who governs the country is not as tyrannical as a non-Muslim”.
The PAS president urged Muslims to fulfil their duty to vote, saying that if they did not turn up, “others” would govern and act according to their own considerations.
In a separate statement, deputy national unity minister R Yuneswaran urged Hadi to withdraw his generalisation portraying non-Muslim rulers as more tyrannical solely because of their religion.
Yuneswaran said leaders had a responsibility not only to defend the interests of their own groups, but also to safeguard the peace, trust and future of all Malaysians.
“Religion is not a licence to be tyrannical, and religious differences are not proof that someone is tyrannical.
“Justice knows no colour, ethnicity or religion. Justice must belong to everyone. Malaysia belongs to all of us. National unity must not be used as a political bargaining chip,” he said.
45dad57436f192f5: MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional candidate for Paya Rumput Rafie Ahmad wants to continue the development initiatives undertaken by the previous assemblyman while addressing residents' concerns over flooding and traffic congestion in the constituency.

Rafie said the issues were among the main complaints raised by residents during the first three days of campaigning, with traffic congestion partly attributed to the large number of traffic lights in the area.
He said he also wanted to address the needs of residents as Paya Rumput continued to experience population growth.

"My hopes for Paya Rumput go beyond seeing taller buildings or wider roads. I want to see our children receive a good education, our young people have opportunities to build their future, mothers have avenues to earn an income, and every family enjoy a better quality of life," he said.
He said development should not be measured solely by physical infrastructure, but also by how much people's lives could be improved.
"Ultimately, development is not just about what we build, but whose lives we manage to improve.

"I do not want to make promises that I may not be able to fulfil. If entrusted with the responsibility, I will do my best to carry it out. I want to continue listening to the community, learning from shortcomings and working towards solutions," he said.
Rafie said he was ready to shoulder the responsibility and work with the people, regardless of their race, age or background, to make Paya Rumput a better place to live and raise future generations.
He said cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and PN under the Muafakat Melaka slogan had given their campaign machinery an advantage, with both sides working together to reach out to voters.
He said the approach was important as Paya Rumput had more than 46,000 voters from various ethnic backgrounds.
Of the total, more than 30,000 were Malay voters, while over 13,000 were Chinese and nearly 3,000 were Indian.
"We do not differentiate based on race, religion or background. Instead, we work fairly for all communities, be they Malay, Chinese or Indian," he said.
Rafie is facing a three-cornered contest in Paya Rumput against Pakatan Harapan candidate Datuk Azman Abidin and Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Parti Bersama Malaysia.
In the 2021 Melaka election, BN's Datuk Rais Yasin won the seat with 6,830 votes.
For this election, the seat was allocated to PN as part of the cooperation between BN and PN, while Rais is contesting in Sungai Udang.
b50b7b87ee2c8f6a: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The High Court here today dismissed an application by the son of the late Genting heiress Lim Siew Kim to remove two interim administrators overseeing the RM1.6 billion estate.
Judge Datuk Mahazan Mat Taib dismissed Marcus Chan Jau Chwen’s application against lawyer Datuk S. Satharuban and Khoo Siew Kiat and ordered him to pay RM30,000 in costs to the two administrators.
The court also discharged the interim injunction restraining the two from acting as administrators of the estate, allowing them to resume their duties under the court’s supervision.

In her ruling, Mahzan said Marcus had failed to establish misconduct, persistent breaches of duty, a disqualifying conflict of interest or other sufficiently serious circumstances to justify their removal.

“I find that Marcus has failed to establish sufficient grounds for the removal of the joint administrators pendente lite. However, dismissing the application does not amount to blanket approval of every expenditure or transaction undertaken by the administrators.
“Their obligations to account for estate assets, comply with the appointment order and submit their costs and remuneration for examination remain unaffected,” she said.

On allegations of interference in companies linked to the estate, Mahazan said the administrators could not classify the companies’ liabilities as debts of the estate simply on the basis that Siew Kim held shares in those entities.

However, she said they remained responsible for safeguarding the estate’s interests, which could include obtaining relevant information and taking lawful action to protect the value of its shareholdings.
The judge also ruled that the evidence was insufficient to establish unlawful interference in the companies’ affairs or misuse of estate funds warranting the administrators’ removal.
She clarified that the decision did not address the validity of Siew Kim’s will or determine the beneficiaries’ entitlements.

Siew Kim, who died of cancer in July 2022 at the age of 73, left behind three daughters and a son. Her estate has since been administered by interim administrators amid an ongoing family dispute over the validity of her will.
On November 27, 2023, the High Court appointed Satharuban Sivasubramaniam and Khoo as administrators pendente lite to oversee the estate.

Their appointment followed a probate suit filed by two of Siew Kim’s daughters, Chan T’shiao Li and Kimberly Chan T’shiao Miin, on January 19, 2023, challenging the validity of a will said to have been executed on April 28, 2022.

Marcus, Siew Kim’s only son and a 30 per cent beneficiary of the residuary estate, sought the removal of both administrators, alleging misconduct and non-compliance with the court order governing their appointment.

Among his complaints were allegations that certain payments had been made to solicitors and other parties through individual bank accounts instead of consolidated trust accounts, resulting in the wrongful depletion of estate funds.
He also accused the administrators of interfering in the management of companies linked to the estate.

Marcus further alleged that the administrators had nearly caused the estate to pay RM4.73 million in assessments on behalf of Prominview Sdn Bhd, although the liability allegedly rested with a joint-venture partner.

Other complaints included the lodging of private caveats and the commissioning of property valuations despite the administrators allegedly having no authority to distribute or dispose of estate assets.
On January 23, 2026, Marcus obtained an ad interim injunction restraining the administrators from acting on behalf of the estate pending the disposal of his application to remove them. — Bernama

219677e4f409c3f8: KUALA LUMPUR: Social media personality Dr Afifah Hidayah Ahmad Tawfek, 36, widely known as Dr Fie, has issued a public apology after drawing flak online for an allegedly insensitive reaction during a recent livestream.

The controversy erupted during a TikTok Live broadcast when she responded to a viewer's comment about the late Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, a former pilot employed by her husband, entrepreneur Captain Amrul Nizar Anuar.
Captain Zainol tragically died in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Miri, Sarawak, on Sep 8 while still awaiting unpaid wages.
Taking to Threads to address the uproar, Dr Fie admitted she had erred in how the moment came across.

"I apologise for the mistake. I am not a perfect human being. I also have flaws," she wrote, reminding critics that "behind the name currently being talked about is a human being with a heart, a family, and dignity to protect."
Clarifying her viral reaction, she insisted she was not making light of the tragedy, explaining that her expression was purely out of shock at her husband's off-the-cuff remark.

"I would never have the heart to laugh at a sensitive issue. I was simply shocked by Cap's (Captain Amrul) spontaneous answer. No one is being spiteful. I feel sorry for the late Zainol's wife," she added.
Rather than trading barbs with her detractors, Dr Fie urged the public to exercise restraint and empathy online.
"I choose not to respond to hatred with hatred. May Allah protect our hearts from judging too quickly, and may we never be the reason someone is hurt by our words," she said.
The issue of delayed pilot salaries at Captain Amrul's company had previously been brought to light by the late pilot's former wife.
bb8fc0565431c60c: LONDON: Bitcoin fell below US$70,000 Friday for the first time since August, extending a two-day slump to as much as 9% as concerns about inflation and higher interest rates weighed on cryptocurrencies.

The largest digital asset sank as much as 5.4% to US$67,628, its lowest level since Aug 19, adding to a 3.8% decline on Thursday. It later pared some losses to trade around US$69,000 at 7.30 am in London. Asian stocks erased an earlier tech-led advance while bonds slumped, with investors remaining cautious ahead of US producer-price data.
Roughly US$1.5 billion in bullish bets on cryptocurrencies were liquidated over a 24-hour period, according to CoinGlass data. Forced selling by leveraged traders added momentum to the decline.

“Once it broke below US$70,000, over US$1 billion of leveraged longs were forced out, which fed more selling,” said Sean McNulty, a derivatives trader at market maker AQC Tech. Ether, the second-largest token, fell as much as 6%, bringing it back under US$2,000.

Bitcoin’s weakness reflects a convergence of macro pressures on crypto in recent weeks. Elevated oil prices and persistent inflation have reinforced expectations for additional US Federal Reserve rate increases. Democrats retaking both chambers of the US Congress next year following the midterm elections has raised expectations of greater regulatory scrutiny on the industry.

This week, a key gauge of US consumer prices posted another firm advance in October, keeping the Fed on track to raise rates next month. The consumer price index, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% from a month earlier, topping estimates for a third straight month. Overall prices jumped 0.4% as the cost of essentials climbed across the board.

“If the Fed hikes rates by 50 basis points rather than the expected 25 basis points, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies could have more room to fall,” said Jeff Mei, chief operating officer of crypto exchange BTSE.

Rich Rosenblum, co-founder of crypto market maker GSR, said volatility in the artificial intelligence trade and continued US dollar strength have washed out some long Bitcoin positions, while the hot inflation data and changes in Nvidia’s leadership are also dragging on risk assets.
Institutional buyers have also been on the retreat for the past two weeks. Since Oct 30, US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have seen more than US$2.5 billion in net outflows.
7548eb3960d07918: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional are "leading" their opponents in 24 of the 28 state seats in Melaka, think tank Ilham Centre said.

In a survey released on the eve of the Melaka polls, Ilham Centre attributed the BN-PN dominance to the acceptance level of their electoral partnership, their effective grassroots machinery, and high approval ratings for the state government.
Its findings showed that 91% of PN supporters were willing to vote for BN candidates, while 78% of BN supporters were prepared to back the PN candidates.
“These factors make it increasingly difficult for PH to penetrate 23 Malay-majority seats,” the report by the think tank said.
The survey also found that caretaker chief minister Ab Rauf Yusoh enjoyed an 86% approval rating, while the BN-led state government recorded 85% approval.

Ilham Centre attributed the ratings partly to the state government's Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat and Jelajah Ketua Menteri Sayang Rakyat programmes, which it said increased voter confidence through direct engagement and assistance.
It also found that the BN-PN campaign slogan, "Asal Bukan PH" (Anyone But PH), had gained traction among the Malay voters.
Ilham Centre said Pakatan Harapan had a comfortable lead in only two of its traditional strongholds - Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir.
Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir will see three-cornered contests which will also feature BN and Bersama.
The Ayer Keroh and Kesidang seats, both previously held by PH, will be closely contested, it said.
Ayer Keroh will see a four-cornered fight, while Kesidang will witness a three-cornered contest.
Ilham Cenre said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) between the government and Bersatu had failed to translate into effective electoral cooperation at the grassroots level.
Unlike the arrangement between BN and PN, it said, the government-Bersatu understanding lacked a common electoral message and effective mechanisms for transferring voter support.

Bersatu president Muhyiddin Yassin and five other MPs from the party signed the CSA last month, giving them access to constituency development funds that government MPs have had access to for the past four years.

Ilham Centre also found that 21% of voters below 30 remained undecided at the time of the survey, held from Nov 1 to 12, involving 805 respondents across all 28 constituencies, alongside focus group discussions and in-depth interviews.
It said most of these voters would decide who to cast their ballots for at the last minute after assessing the candidates and parties.
"We believe that this group is also likely to gravitate towards the blue wave," it said, referring to BN and PN.
201b2c9d34652f71: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today fixed Nov 24 to hear an application by two lawyers to discharge themselves from representing comedian and actor Harith Iskander in a defamation suit filed by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor.
"Yes, we have applied to discharge ourselves from representing (Harith Iskander)," lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo said when contacted.

She and co-counsel Harkiranjit Kaur Manjit Singh attended online case management proceedings before judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi today, alongside Rosmah's lawyers, Mohamed Baharudeen Mohamed Ariff and Nur-Diana Ezlyn Hashim.
Baharudeen said the Nov 24 hearing will be conducted online via Zoom at 2.15pm.

Rosmah, 74, filed the defamation suit through Messrs Hafarizam & Aisha Mubarak against Harith Iskander Musa, 60, on June 9, claiming he insulted and body-shamed her during his stand-up comedy show, Harith Iskander: The Outspoken Comedy Tour, at a hotel in Melaka on Jan 17.

In her statement of claim, the former prime minister's wife alleged that Harith Iskander showed an image of frightening mythical creatures before displaying her photograph, followed by remarks mocking the idea of looking in the rear-view mirror while driving along a dark road.

She claimed a TikTok user uploaded a recording of the performance, which garnered hundreds of thousands of views and damaged her reputation and dignity as a public figure and patron of charitable organisations.

Rosmah is seeking general, aggravated and exemplary damages, an injunction to prevent the statements from being republished, and a written apology in two mainstream newspapers and on social media accounts.

In his statement of defence filed on July 9, Harith Iskander denied that the image was defamatory, saying the TikTok clip was published without his knowledge or consent and did not reflect the full context of the performance.
7445d4050c417092: KUALA LUMPUR: Agama sepatutnya menjadi asas penyatuan masyarakat, bukannya dijadikan sentimen untuk memecah-belahkan rakyat, kata Ketua Setiausaha Pakatan Harapan (PH), Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Menurutnya, Islam tidak menjadi mulia dengan merendahkan agama lain, sebaliknya melalui keadilan, akhlak, ilmu, amanah dan contoh kepimpinan yang baik.
Beliau menegaskan, kekuatan orang Melayu dan umat Islam tidak akan terhakis hanya kerana menghormati hak kaum serta agama lain.
Sehubungan itu, beliau berkata, kenyataan Presiden PAS Hadi Awang melabel pemimpin bukan Islam sebagai zalim amat dikesali kerana meletakkan ukuran keadilan dan kezaliman berdasarkan agama seseorang.
"Sungguh amat dikesali ada yang membuat kesimpulan bahawa orang Islam yang zalim tetap lebih baik daripada orang bukan Islam, hanya kerana perbezaan agama?
"Seseorang pemimpin tidak hanya dinilai berdasarkan identiti agamanya semata-mata, tetapi berdasarkan amanah, keadilan dan keupayaannya melindungi rakyat," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Beliau berkata, rasuah, penindasan dan pengkhianatan terhadap amanah tetap suatu kesalahan tanpa mengira siapa pelakunya.

Ketika berucap di pentas Grand Finale Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) menjelang PRN Melaka semalam, Hadi menegaskan dalam Islam, perkiraan politik dibuat berlandaskan faktor dosa dan pahala berbanding orang bukan Islam yang didakwanya 'zalim'
"Sejahat-jahat orang Islam, seburuk-buruk orang Islam memerintah negara, mereka tidak sezalim orang bukan Islam," katanya.

Susulan itu, pemimpin DAP Selangor, S Preakas, menggesa Hadi menarik balik kenyataan tersebut, sambil mempersoalkan sama ada salah guna wang rakyat menjadi kurang serius hanya kerana pelakunya beragama Islam.

Beliau berkata, kenyataan Hadi dalam ceramah kempen di Bukit Katil, Melaka itu bukan sahaja menghina rakyat bukan Islam, malah merendahkan tuntutan amanah yang perlu dipikul setiap pemimpin tanpa mengira agama.
Justeru, beliau meminta Umno, MCA, MIC dan Gerakan menyatakan pendirian terhadap kenyataan itu, selain menggesa Hadi memohon maaf secara terbuka kepada rakyat bukan Islam.
26d6277f47d1bbd8: KUALA LUMPUR: The political temperature remains normal despite the Melaka election, and the cabinet meeting proceeded as usual without any problems, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
"The political temperature out there is ordinary.
"When there is an election, the temperature rises for a while, then drops again," he said.
Anwar said the weekly cabinet meeting had proceeded as usual.
"The meeting just now was normal. I did not detect any problems.
"The only thing was the absence of the Transport Minister (Anthony Loke), who has resigned," he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Madrasathul Gouthiyyah Surau in Brickfields.
He said both Deputy Prime Ministers, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, and the other ministers were present.
"Both deputy prime ministers were present at the cabinet meeting, along with the other ministers. Our discussion focused on development and facilities for the people," he said.

On Wednesday, Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, challenged Barisan Nasional (BN) members of parliament to resign from the cabinet rather than continue criticising the prime minister and the unity government.
Zahid, who is also BN chairman, said on Tuesday Parliament should be dissolved and the mandate returned to the people instead of reshuffling the cabinet.
Voters in Melaka will head to the polls on Saturday, with 687,697 registered voters eligible to cast their ballots at 240 polling stations across the state.
1e4ec508eb1a1c86: PUTRAJAYA: Drainage maintenance in Selangor will be stepped up immediately as an interim measure to reduce the frequency of flash floods while flood mitigation projects carried out.

Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had briefed the cabinet today on a special meeting he chaired yesterday to address recurring floods in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor.

He said the meeting was briefed that drainage maintenance in Kuala Lumpur was carried out six times a year, and that Selangor needed to increase its maintenance frequency, particularly in flood hotspots.
He said funding and allocations had already been provided for flood mitigation projects in Selangor, with work currently underway, although completion would take time.
Anwar yesterday chaired a special meeting in Parliament with Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari to improve coordination in tackling recurring floods in the state.

The meeting focused on four key actions, including strengthening early warning systems with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and improving coordination through the Selangor Disaster Management Committee.
As of 8am today, the number of flood evacuees in Selangor had risen to 1,248 people from 338 families at seven relief centres, compared with 1,144 people from 318 families yesterday evening.

1e029f2741315e16: For all the supposed improvements, inspectors still obsess over statistics and adjectives, but surely school success depends on teachers and parents The government regulation of state schools by Ofsted in England is a fiasco. Following the 2023 suicide of the Reading headteacher Ruth Perry, after her school was downgraded from outstanding to inadequate, Ofsted appears to have referred to a dictionary. Single words were replaced by colour-coded report cards, which use a wider range of different adjectives to grade abstractions such as personal development and wellbeing, achievement and leadership. Never has the concept of “education” seemed so empty. The reaction of the teaching profession to the new code has itself been devastating, as highlighted in a recent survey that showed more than half of headteachers in England polled after their schools were inspected under Ofsted’s new regime are now considering early retirement as a result of the experience. This sense of misery was also illustrated in a poll conducted by the National Education Union one year on from the introduction of the new framework, with 65% saying it is the same as or worse than before. Simon Jenkins is a Guardian columnist In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. 8e6c40ca478935be: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award revivals a healthy revival It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player. You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball. These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds. fd63485d4a06ea59: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Umno has urged DAP to resolve its differences with coalition partners through dialogue and consultation, instead of issuing public ultimatums or demanding resignations, following the controversy over Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon.

Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, described DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo’s call for Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to resign if he did not support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s leadership, as regrettable and unhelpful to the unity government’s stability.
“Issuing public ultimatums to the president of a coalition partner is neither constructive nor consistent with the spirit of the Coalition Agreement,” she said in a statement today.

Azalina, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), said the agreement did not require coalition partners to agree unconditionally with every political position taken by the prime minister or other political leaders.
She outlined four options for DAP, including invoking the agreement’s mediation mechanism, allowing existing arrangements to continue or seeking a review of the agreement.
She said terminating it would ultimately point towards the dissolution of Parliament, as it contained no provision for termination before the end of the 15th Parliament.

On Najib’s conditional pardon, Azalina said the exercise of the royal prerogative of mercy under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution should not be portrayed as a unilateral political decision by any party.
She also defended Umno’s continued participation in the unity government, saying the party would honour its commitments, respect Anwar’s leadership and uphold the Federal Constitution.
“We have made our position clear. The next move is yours,” she said.
c2f5d1de981ea623: SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The police are awaiting instructions from the office of the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) regarding 15 more cases of individuals impersonating the aide-de-camp (ADC) of the Raja Muda of Selangor in vehicle and property transactions.

Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said that 17 investigation papers have been opened based on the police reports received, and all of them have been completed before being referred to the Selangor DPP office for further instructions.
“Yesterday and today, the DPP agreed to charge a male and female suspect in court under Section 109 and Section 420 of the Penal Code.

“As for the other 15 cases, the police are waiting for feedback from the DPP’s office for any further instructions,” he said at the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) media conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) here today.

Earlier, the media reported that Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, pleaded guilty while another accused, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, pleaded not guilty at the Klang Magistrate’s Court on charges of fraud involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM40,000 in April.
Yesterday, both the accused recorded their pleas at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court regarding the charge of fraud involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM30,000 in May.

The police had previously confirmed the arrest of a man believed to be the main suspect in a vehicle and residential sales fraud case using the image of the Raja Muda of Selangor around Johor Bahru on October 27.
Commenting further, Shazeli said the investigation found nearly 27 cases reported nationwide, including 17 in Selangor, with estimated losses amounting to RM1.4 million.

He also expressed appreciation to the public who came forward to cooperate in providing information until the suspect was brought to justice and advised the public to be vigilant to avoid becoming victims of fraud.

Meanwhile, Shazeli said his team also successfully dismantled two online fraud syndicates or ‘call centres’ with the arrest of 11 individuals in two operations in Sungai Long, Kajang and Taman Aman Perdana on November 3 and 10 respectively.
“The syndicate, which has been operating since September, targets foreigners living abroad as victims by offering them investment schemes and ‘love scams’.
“All the suspects, including 10 foreign nationals, aged 22 to 45, acted as customer service operators. The police also seized various equipment worth RM20,000,” he added. — Bernama
a27cf9485640fb34: PUTRAJAYA: Islam is not elevated by putting down other religions, but through justice, good morals, knowledge, integrity and exemplary leadership, says Pakatan Harapan (PH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the strength of the Malays and Muslims would not be diminished by respecting the rights of other races and religions.
"I take seriously the statement that even the worst Muslim leader governing the country is not as oppressive as a non-Muslim leader, as reportedly made during a political ceramah in Melaka.

"Such a statement is regrettable because it judges a leader's justice or oppression based on religion rather than morals, integrity, actions and sense of responsibility," he said in a statement today.
He said Islam taught its followers to uphold justice even towards those they disliked, as stated in verse eight of Surah al-Maidah.
"And do not let your hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just, for that is closer to righteousness," he said, quoting the verse.
Saifuddin said leaders should be judged by their integrity, commitment to justice and ability to protect the people, rather than their religious identity.
The home minister said corruption, oppression and betrayal of trust were wrong regardless of who committed them, adding that religion should not be used to shield corrupt leaders.
He added that Muslims would earn greater respect by setting an example through justice, progress, wisdom and compassion towards all humanity.

Elections, he said, should allow voters to assess the track records, integrity and capabilities of candidates and political parties, rather than become a platform for stoking racial and religious fears and prejudice.

Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang was reported to have described non-Muslims as oppressive during a speech at the Grand Finale of the Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) rallies ahead of the Melaka state election.
He said political considerations in Islam were based on the concepts of sin and reward. — BERNAMA
bf782657f5d18f02: Suspect held in New York jail has been linked to handler behind Iran-linked operations in Britain When the US took custody of Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi in May, investigators hoped the string of terrorist and arson attacks he was accused of promoting and directing against American and Jewish targets in the UK and Europe on behalf of Iran would stop. They were wrong. An updated indictment, released on Tuesday by the US Department of Justice, describes some of what happened next. It reveals that al-Saadi has two allies, believed to be in Iran, also trying to provoke fear and chaos in the UK, one of whom is accused of orchestrating the September incident at RAF Fairford.
