c4a5fe405b55e617: TOKYO: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group and Mizuho Financial Group on Friday raised their profit forecasts for the financial year but flagged the prospect of a slowdown in investment into AI data centres.

SMFG boosted its annual earnings forecast to 1.9 trillion yen from 1.7 trillion yen and expanded its share buyback programme as corporate lending demand from local firms remained strong and higher domestic interest rates increased lending margins.

Net profit over the July to September quarter was 501.8 billion yen (US$3.14 billion), down 10 per cent from a year earlier, when it registered a gain of 94 billion yen on the sale of its stake in India's Kotak Mahindra Bank.

Mizuho also raised its annual profit forecast to 1.6 trillion yen from 1.4 trillion yen and doubled the size of its share buyback programme this financial year to 400 billion yen. The company generated 473.6 billion yen (US$2.96 billion) in net profit over the July to September period, 19 per cent higher than the year before.
A slowdown in data centre investment could hit the Japanese and global economies and impact SMFG's results over the next six months, chief executive officer Toru Nakashima said at a press briefing.
"This year we have adopted stricter standards on extending credit for data centre financing, for instance restricting ourselves to just hyperscalers with high credit standing," Nakashima said.

Mizuho CEO Masahiro Kihara flagged greater restrictions on data centre construction in the US as a tail risk as the results of the midterm elections last week brought sweeping wins for the Democratic Party, which could slow projects and so bring about higher development costs.

Fears of overheating in global data centre investment and rising political opposition have led to a sharp decline in technology stocks in recent weeks as investors reassess their exposure to the vast sums flowing into AI infrastructure.

The resignation of the chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, over extramarital affairs has sparked concern over the chipmaker's continued ability to spearhead data centre projects as it both supplies chips and finances the infrastructure built around them.
"The impact of Huang stepping down is difficult to see at present and whether it leads to a slowdown in data centre investment will depend on the new management," SMFG's Nakashima said.
"Personally, I don't think their stance will change that significantly," he added.
SMFG increased its share buyback programme by 220 billion yen, bringing the total shares to be bought up to 400 billion yen for the financial year that ends in March 2027.
3cd682b993fcb5ae: KUALA LUMPUR: A Singaporean businessman pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court to a charge of criminal breach of trust involving 500,000 shares belonging to a company, four years ago.
Poh Po Lian, 68, entered the plea after the charge was read out to him before Judge Rosli Ahmad.

According to the charge, Poh, together with another person who remains at large, allegedly committed criminal breach of trust regarding shares in Victoria Island Club Bhd which had been entrusted to them by Tan Sri Ta Kin Yan by transferring them to Jennifer Kok Sau Keng without the consent of six individuals who were entitled to receive a portion of those shares.
The act was allegedly committed at a residential unit in Solaris Dutamas, Jalan Dutamas 1 on July 31, 2022.
The charge is brought under Section 406 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years' jail, whipping, and a fine, upon conviction.
Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Dr Ifa Sirrhu Samsudin proposed bail at RM1 million with two sureties, one of whom must be a Malaysian citizen with a permanent address in the country.

"The prosecution also recommends an additional condition for the accused to report to the nearest Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office once a month and is prohibited from interfering with any witnesses in this case.

"We do not intend to request that the accused's passport be impounded, given that he is a foreign national and the document is essential for his travel to and from Singapore. Given these factors, we believe a bail amount of RM1 million is appropriate," he said.

Lawyer Datuk Jerald Gomez, representing Poh, requested a lower bail amount, noting that his client holds a pass under the 'Malaysia My Second Home' (MM2H) programme, having resided and conducted business in Malaysia for over 30 years.

"My client owns various companies and assets in Malaysia. He also possesses properties in strategic locations across the country, including at Pavilion Bukit Bintang and in Penang. There is no flight risk," he said.

Judge Rosli granted bail at RM400,000 with two Malaysian sureties, and imposed additional conditions that the accused must not interfere with prosecution witnesses and must report to the nearest Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission office once a month.
The court has set Dec 8 for the next mention of the case. — BERNAMA
ea4b529ba89fd40b: PETALING JAYA: Umno mencadangkan empat pilihan untuk pertimbangan DAP susulan ketidakpuasan hati parti itu berhubung tahanan di rumah yang diberikan kepada Najib Razak.
Ketua Penerangan Umno Azalina Othman Said berkata pilihan pertama adalah DAP mengusahakan pengantaraan dalam kalangan parti komponen kerajaan.

Katanya, fasal 5(c) dalam perjanjian kerajaan perpaduan membolehkan proses pengantaraan melalui majlis perundingan, dianggotai wakil-wakil parti komponen, bagi menyelesaikan sebarang pertikaian atau salah faham.
Bagaimanapun, Azalina tertanya-tanya mengapa DAP tidak mengusahakan pengantaraan lebih awal, sedangkan pengampunan Najib diketahui umum sejak Januari 2024.
Sementara itu, pilihan kedua adalah menamatkan perjanjian kerajaan perpaduan.
Azalina bagaimanapun berkata fasal sedemikian tidak wujud memandangkan perjanjian itu adalah untuk sehingga tamat penggal Parlimen ke-15.
"Oleh itu, kesimpulan yang jelas di sini adalah pembubaran Parlimen," katanya.
Atau, DAP boleh mengambil pilihan ketiga iaitu bertenang dan membenarkan aturan sedia ada diteruskan.

Azalina berkata DAP sendiri pernah mendapat manfaat daripada prerogatif belas kasihan diraja pada 2018, yang merujuk kepada pengampunan yang diberikan kepada Anwar Ibrahim, serta titah diraja pada 2022, yang memudahkan pembentukan kerajaan perpaduan.
"Peristiwa-peristiwa itu menekankan betapa pentingnya menghormati peranan institusi beraja dalam Perlembagaan serta prerogatif belas kasihan diraja," katanya.
Akhir sekali, DAP boleh memohon perjanjian kerajaan perpaduan disemak semula, khususnya perenggan C, berkenaan ikrar parti komponen untuk mendukung Perlembagaan termasuk institusi raja-raja Melayu.
"Sebarang pertimbangan oleh DAP untuk menyemak semula perenggan C akan mengundang akibat yang tidak dapat dijangka terhadap kesinambungan kerajaan perpaduan," katanya.
Kenyataan Azalina ini menyusuli cabaran Pengerusi DAP Gobind Singh Deo agar Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi meletak jawatan sekiranya beliau tidak menyokong kepimpinan Anwar sebagai perdana menteri.

Kenyataan Gobind itu menjawab kenyataan Zahid bahawa pembubaran Parlimen adalah lebih baik berbanding rombakan Jemaah Menteri, susulan peletakan jawatan Setiausaha Agung DAP Loke Siew Fook sebagai menteri pengangkutan.

Peletakan jawatan Loke berkaitan pengampunan bersyarat yang diberikan kepada Najib. Peletakan jawatan dibuat pada September dan berkuat kuasa selepas bekas presiden Umno itu memulakan tahanan di rumah, awal minggu ini.
Azalina berkata kenyataan Gobind itu amat dikesali dan tidak membantu mengukuhkan semangat kerjasama dalam kerajaan perpaduan.
Beliau menambah kata dua secara terbuka kepada presiden parti yang bersama dalam kerajaan adalah tindakan yang tidak membina serta tidak selaras dengan semangat perjanjian kerajaan perpaduan.
"Jika terdapat perbezaan pendapat dalam kalangan rakan, tindakan yang wajar adalah melalui dialog dan perundingan, bukannya menekan-nekan di khalayak atau mendesak peletakan jawatan," katanya.
Azalina berkata Umno akan terus menghormati komitmen yang telah dibuat, menghormati kepimpinan Anwar, serta mempertahankan Perlembagaan.
"Kami telah menyatakan pendirian kami dengan jelas. Langkah seterusnya terserah kepada anda."
738b382586147fd3: LONDON: Faisa Omar applied for more than 500 jobs in the UK and got nowhere -- a slog she likened to "shouting into the void". It took a 10-week training course, tailored to the green energy sector, to finally land her a job within a month.

Her story is one the Labour government hopes to replicate on a much bigger scale, as it prepares to receive a report and proposals next week that would, controversially, restrict youth sickness and disability benefits in order to fund back-to-work programmes aimed at the nearly 1 million young people not in work, education or training.

Britain had 981,000 people aged 16-24 not in employment, education or training (NEET) in the second quarter of this year, accounting for 13% of the age group as a whole and a share that was the second-highest in Europe last year.

Its 15.6% youth unemployment rate is also unusually high compared with the 3.4% rate for older workers — elsewhere in Europe, the youth jobless rate is typically only just over double that of older age groups.
Former minister Alan Milburn, a party ally of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, warned of a "lost generation" in May in the first part of his report into youth unemployment.

Disagreement is likely to arise over Milburn's plans for how to fund more back-to-work programmes against a backdrop of stretched public finances, something he addressed in a newspaper interview on Thursday.
"I'm not saying that any of this will be easy, or that it will be pain-free," Milburn told the Times. "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support."

Milburn said earlier this year that he wanted to shift the 25-to-1 ratio of spending on benefits versus employment support more towards the latter, and draw lessons from the Netherlands and elsewhere where more young people are in work.
Next week he will propose barring under-25s from ill-health supplements to standard unemployment benefits and also moving them to a more restricted version of the main disability benefit.
But his report is unlikely to rapidly reduce the £8 billion a year spent on benefits for young people.

Cuts are also likely to be unpopular among many lawmakers in the Labour Party who thwarted attempts by previous prime minister Keir Starmer to cut welfare, handing ammunition to opposition parties who accuse the governing party of favouring welfare recipients over workers.
UK employment problem
Michael Houlihan, UK head of employment charity Generation, said programmes with a proven track record in getting people into jobs should be scaled up.

Around 70% of people on Generation's courses found a job within 12 months, double the average for similar ones, he said, with the key being to ensure courses were tailored to the precise needs of employers in sectors with vacancies.
For 27-year-old Omar, attending a course in 2023 at Generation focused on specific roles in green energy helped her nail down a job within a month.

"Before Generation I had the drive but I didn't have the map. So I didn't know how to get into sustainability. Climate change was one of my passions, but I didn't know how to ... find an accessible path into the green sector," he said.

One part of the problem now, according to James Tuttiett, an executive at IT consultancy FDM Group, is that artificial intelligence has reduced client demand for junior staff. He said FDM now had to train recruits for longer before hiring them out.

"You have this silent hiring freeze where AI can increasingly do a lot of jobs that exist in white-collar work," he said, adding that a higher minimum wage and increased employer social security payments had also limited hiring.
Less back-to-work support
So-called NEETs' reasons for not being in work or training vary, but many lack educational qualifications or report having health conditions that make it harder to get a job.

Nye Cominetti, an economist at the left-leaning Resolution Foundation think tank, said Britain's welfare benefits were not unusually generous compared with European countries with lower rates of NEETs. But young people receiving health-related benefits in Britain faced fewer requirements to engage with a process of getting back to work.

Sonja Bekker, a professor of employment law at Utrecht University in the Netherlands, said her city sent people to knock on the doors of young people not in education or work, to offer solutions such as childcare or mental health support.
Vocational schools mean many Dutch pupils are on months-long work placements aged 17, and two-thirds of 16- to 17-year-olds have part-time jobs — compared with less than a fifth in Britain.
Even in the Netherlands, though, the rate of NEETs has begun to rise. Like in Britain, AI and taxes are sometimes blamed.
"We don't know whether it is a long-term trend or whether it is just a bump in the economic cycle," Bekker said.
8acd2bef1a470686: MELAKA: PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang has reminded Malay voters in Melaka to take part in the state election tomorrow, warning that division and failure to vote could result in a loss of Malay-Muslim political power.
Hadi expressed concern that Malays would stay away from the polls while non-Muslims would turn out in large numbers.

“When the Malays are divided, political power is lost. That is why unity is so important,” he told reporters at the home of Yasin Sarif, the father of Barisan Nasional's Sungai Udang candidate, Rais Yasin.
Hadi said the mutual understanding between BN and Perikatan Nasional in Melaka, particularly on seat allocations, had strengthened their cooperation.
He said Umno was contesting more seats because it was strong in the state, while PAS and PN were not overly concerned about how many seats they were contesting.
“We compromise. Melaka is an Umno stronghold, so PAS is not overly eager to contest many seats. We have agreed that when Umno takes power in Melaka, PAS will join the government,” he said.
Hadi said PAS's priority was to strengthen the position of the Malays before inviting “non-extremist” non-Malay communities, including those represented by MCA and MIC, to work with them.
He also instructed PAS members to vote for the MCA, MIC and Gerakan candidates contesting under the BN-PN pact.
Hadi said racial politics were forbidden and Malay leadership could not be used as an excuse to oppress non-Muslim communities.

He also challenged those who sought to instil fear in non-Malays visiting Kelantan and Terengganu, saying both states were peaceful and non-Muslims there were treated fairly under the PAS administration.
55f2452fdb4e4a3f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The High Court here today fixed November 24 to hear an application by lawyers Sangeet Kaur Deo and Harkiranjit Kaur Manjit Singh to discharge themselves from representing comedian and actor Harith Iskander in a defamation suit filed by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor.
“Yes, we have applied to discharge ourselves from representing (Harith Iskander),” Sangeet confirmed when contacted.

The case management proceedings for the application were held online today before Judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi, with Sangeet and Harkiranjit attending alongside Rosmah’s lawyers, Mohamed Baharudeen Mohamed Ariff and Nur-Diana Ezlyn Hashim.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Baharudeen told reporters that the hearing of the application on November 24 would be conducted online via Zoom at 2.15pm.

Rosmah, 74, filed a defamation suit through Messrs Hafarizam & Aisha Mubarak against Harith Iskander Musa, 60, on June 9, claiming he insulted and body-shamed her during his stand-up comedy performance, Harith Iskander: The Outspoken Comedy Tour, at a hotel in Melaka on January 17.

The former Prime Minister’s wife claimed in her statement of claim that the defendant had shown an image of frightening mythical creatures before displaying her image, followed by remarks mocking the idea of looking in the rear-view mirror while driving along a dark road.

Rosmah also alleged that a TikTok user uploaded a recording of the performance, which garnered hundreds of thousands of views and damaged her reputation and dignity as a public figure and patron of charitable organisations.

In the suit, she is seeking general, aggravated, and exemplary damages; an injunction to prevent the statements from being republished; and a written apology in two mainstream newspapers and on social media accounts.

However, in his statement of defence filed on July 9, Harith Iskander denied that the image was defamatory, adding that the TikTok clip was published without his knowledge or consent and did not reflect the full context of the comedy performance. — Bernama
4c0201e2111453dc: MOSCOW, Nov 13 — US Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott sent an official letter to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang demanding that he appear at a public hearing on December 3 regarding media reports of his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of spying for the Chinese government, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.

“I am writing to request that you voluntarily appear before the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs on December 3, 2026 for a public hearing regarding recent public reports that raise significant national security concerns,” the senator wrote in the letter sent to Huang yesterday evening.

The footnotes of the document referred to recent reports of The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal saying that Chinese business executive Alice Huang had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
The senator warned that the Committee is ready to use all its powers and authority, including subpoenas, if Huang does not appear at the hearing.
The New York Times also reported, citing two sources familiar with the matter, that US President Donald Trump called Huang on Tuesday before his resignation and urged him to fight for his job.
Yesterday, Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation. The Chinese Foreign Ministry has dismissed China’s role in the alleged espionage involving Nvidia as “groundless”. — Bernama-Sputnik/RIA Novosti
2c89c3e3199248c8: KUALA LUMPUR: The sessions court here has fixed Jan 20 to decide on former Perlis menteri besar Azlan Man's false claims and money laundering cases over return flight tickets and hotel stays.
Judge Azura Alwi fixed the date after hearing submissions from deputy public prosecutors Nuralis Mat and Haresh Prakash Somiah, and Azlan's lawyer, Burhanudeen Abdul Wahid, today.
Azlan is charged with five counts of submitting false claims of up to RM1.18 million, and another five money laundering charges amounting to RM1.06 million.
He faces five alternative charges of misappropriation of property amounting to RM1.06 million.
If found guilty of submitting the false claims, he will face a jail term of below 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the RM1.18 million.
The penalty for money laundering is a jail term of below 15 years and a fine of less than RM5 million.
For dishonest misappropriation, Azlan will face a jail term of between six months and five years as well as a fine, if convicted.
Earlier today, Nuralis told the court that Azlan ought to answer all the charges against him.

She said evidence presented by the prosecution had shown that Azlan had, between 2013 and 2017, instructed his then private secretary to cancel the flights and hotel bookings after they were confirmed and paid for by the state government.
The refund from the cancellations was subsequently returned to Azlan's account, she said.
Burhanudeen told the court the state government allocated yearly funds for the menteri besar to travel abroad.
To obtain these funds, he said, Azlan had to engage the services of a travel agent to book the trips.
He said Azlan had been transparent when submitting his travel claims.
"The prosecution claimed that he did not travel and yet submitted claims for it.
"The investigating officer, however, said he undertook those travels on some other dates,” he said.
27e39682d01ab8ce: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Federal Court has fixed February 23 next year to hear the Inland Revenue Board’s (IRB) application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision granting former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against him.
Lawyer Wee Yeong Kang, representing Najib, confirmed the hearing date to Bernama when contacted.
He said the date was fixed during an earlier case management session early this month (November 4).
A further case management session was held today before Federal Court Deputy Registrar Norshakinah Ahmad Kamarudin.

Wee also confirmed that the IRB had not filed an application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision granting a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against Najib’s son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin.

On September 4, the Court of Appeal ruled in favour of Najib and Mohd Nazifuddin, allowing their applications to stay the bankruptcy proceedings pending the disposal of their appeals before the Special Commissioners of Income Tax (SCIT) over additional tax assessments issued by the IRB.
A three-member panel chaired by Justice Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab ruled that the stay was warranted as both appellants had raised specific issues that required determination by the SCIT.

Justice Alwi said there were substantial issues concerning alleged errors in the computation of the taxable amount of approximately RM1.69 billion, including claims of double taxation and the treatment of refunded donations and dividends used for charitable and political purposes.
He noted that the IRB had not disputed the merits of these issues, maintaining instead that they should be properly determined by the SCIT.

The bankruptcy proceedings stemmed from separate High Court decisions granting the IRB’s applications for summary judgment against Najib and his son over unpaid income tax arrears for the 2011 to 2017 assessment years.
The IRB is seeking to recover RM1.69 billion from Najib and RM37.6 million from Mohd Nazifuddin.
Both Najib and Mohd Nazifuddin had previously failed in their appeals before the Court of Appeal and Federal Court to set aside the summary judgments.

Following this, bankruptcy notices were issued against them. They subsequently applied for a stay of the bankruptcy proceedings, but their applications were dismissed by High Court Deputy Registrar Kamarul Aris Kamalluddin on July 29, 2024.
Their subsequent appeals to the High Court were also unsuccessful, prompting them to take the matter to the Court of Appeal, which eventually ruled in their favour.
Najib is currently serving the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at his residence in Kuala Lumpur, following payment of the RM50 million fine.

In September this year, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other stipulated conditions. — Bernama
ab21b6ebe040e3ee: PRAIA: Cape Verde president Jose Maria Neves is expected to win a second term on Sunday, an outcome that would cement full control of government by the island nation’s oldest political party after its victory in legislative elections earlier this year.

Situated more than 600km west of mainland Africa, the former Portuguese colony is home to around only 500,000 people, although it made headlines this year when its men's football team embarked on a fairytale run to the World Cup knockout stage.

Neves' main challenger is Joana Rosa, a former justice minister and Cape Verde's first woman presidential candidate. Analysts put Neves as the clear favourite to win another five years in office, after a race that has highlighted issues like employment and stemming outward migration.
"We must also find ways to ensure that young people can build their futures here at home and prevent the continued exodus of young Cape Verdeans abroad," Rosa told Reuters.
"This outflow creates domestic problems and slows down our development process."
Top candidate vows 'inclusive growth', better wages

Cape Verde, also in the news this year when a cruise ship carrying hantavirus-infected passengers became stranded off its coast, operates under a hybrid presidential-parliamentary model. The prime minister heads the government while the president ​retains significant powers including veto authority and a mediating role.
Neves is backed by the African Party for ​the Independence of Cape Verde (PAICV), which won 37 out of 72 seats in legislative elections in May, allowing Francisco Carvalho to become prime minister.
His opponent Rosa is from the Movement for Democracy party, which had governed for 10 years prior to the legislative vote.

Neves, who served as prime minister for 15 years beginning in 2001, told Reuters he had spent his first term as president trying to reach as many Cape Verdeans as possible, "taking the presidency to the islands" and to the diaspora in Africa and the US.
His goals in a second term would include organising a "Youth Convention" focused on employment needs and a forum to identify development priorities between now and 2050, he said.

"I want to inspire Cape Verdeans and mobilise them to accelerate progress towards inclusive economic growth, while implementing the reforms needed to deliver better wages, higher incomes and an improved quality of life," he said.
Rosa, for her part, said she was running to "demonstrate women's capabilities", attract foreign investment and ensure a balance of power in government instead of total control by PAICV.
b539aacbadadd27c: PETALING JAYA, Nov 13 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has criticised PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over his remarks that even the worst Muslim government is less oppressive than a non-Muslim administration, saying leaders should be judged by their integrity and actions, not religion.
In a statement today, Saifuddin Nasution said such comparisons were regrettable as they risked using religion to divide society and excuse wrongdoing by political leaders.

He said Islam taught Muslims to uphold justice even towards those they disliked, citing verse eight of Surah Al-Maidah, which states: “Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just, for that is closer to righteousness.”
Saifuddin Nasution questioned the suggestion that an oppressive Muslim leader should be considered better than a non-Muslim simply because of their religious identity.
He said a leader’s worth should instead be measured by their trustworthiness, fairness and ability to protect the people under their care.
“Corruption is corruption. Oppression is oppression. Betrayal of trust remains wrongdoing, regardless of who commits it.
“We must not use religion to provide moral protection for corrupt leaders,” he said.
He stressed that Islam’s standing should not be built by belittling other religions.

Saifuddin stressed that Islam’s standing should not be elevated by belittling other religions, adding that respecting the rights of other races and faiths would not weaken the Malay community or Muslims.
Instead, he said Muslims would earn greater respect by setting an example through justice, progress, wisdom and compassion towards all people.
He also said elections should not become platforms for stirring racial and religious fears or prejudice.

His statement followed Hadi’s remarks at the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional grand finale rally in Melaka, where the PAS president urged Muslims to vote, warning that their failure to do so could allow non-Muslims to take power.
ca326b32b3ec013a: The next version of the C++ programming language may be delayed at the last minute due to a dispute over a security-enhancing Contracts feature.

Contracts have deeply split C++ technical maintainers. One group backs the C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup, who is against the technology in its present form in grounds it was hastily implemented. But others are eager to see Contracts implemented, even arguing the tech's detractors are poisoning the C++ development process itself.
The disagreement boiled over just before a vote to ratify the new version of the language.

In October, the Draft International Standard (DIS) of C++26 failed its ISO ballot — the next-to-last stage in the International Organization for Standardization’s approval process during which a standard's technical details are formally ratified by a set of national standards bodies.

The ballot saw 13 votes cast in favor, 9 against, and 12 abstentions, failing to meet the ISO requirement of having no more than 25 percent negative votes. Contracts was the major sticking point for those voting nay.
Contracts dispute

Contracts allow developers to add preconditions and postconditions to code, as well as assertions that check whether specified conditions hold. Such checks can help catch programming errors that might otherwise lead to undefined behavior.
Design by Contract has long been a feature of languages like Ada and Eiffel.
Developers have proposed adding Contracts to C++ for at least a decade, after when they were abruptly yanked from C++20 owing to concerns over dangerous defaults.
But Stroustrup roasted the revised proposal (P2900) that made it into C++26.

“The P2900 contracts and extensions aim to change the nature of C++ and are an existential threat to C++, adding complexity and bloat,” Stroustrup and his colleagues wrote in a paper last August. They noted that the implementation is messy, outdated, not sufficiently tested, and could be more effectively implemented as a library.

Not everyone agrees. Andreas Fertig, a member of the C++ standardization committee, feels that the criticisms have already been vetted and that vetoing the proposal this late in the C++ release process is damaging to C++ itself.

“The topic has been worked on for years and has received a majority vote multiple times in its current form. By voting ‘no,’ an established system, one based primarily on trust and respectful collaboration, has been shaken,” Fertig wrote in a blog post.

The elephant in the room is, of course, the ongoing criticism of how easy it is for developers to accidentally create security holes in C++, leading more than a few projects to adpot Rust. Adding controls might, as Stroustrup notes, hamper C++’s chief attribute of being a blazing-fast language.
Sore losers
Fertig accused Stroustrup and Co. of being sore losers.

“Every ISO standard is simply a set of compromises. Everyone loses sometimes, and everyone wins sometimes,” he wrote. But in this case, “the losing parties refused to accept their loss. The question that primarily determines how to move forward is whether the group can rebuild trust."
Unlike Fertig, Harry Bott, CEO of the C++ Alliance – which maintains the open source EDG C++ compiler front end – does not see the Contracts discussion as disruptive to C++ itself.

“The draft being sent back isn’t a failure of the process—it’s the process working as intended,” he wrote to The Register by email. “That doesn’t mean the process can’t improve. The goal should be to learn from this and strengthen the process so C++ can continue to evolve in a way developers can rely on.”
Where to now?

With the ballot failing at this late point of the standardization process – a rarity in C++ history – the language risks missing its expected shipping date of this year. That outcome may force everyone to refer to the new version as “C++27” rather than C++26. (That’s only the informal name; the official name of this eighth version of the language, should it be released next year, would be “ISO/IEC 14882:2027.”)
ISO C++ working group WG21 is meeting next week in Búzios, Brazil, for the confronto final.
According to a blog post from Thibault Ricord-Marchal, a software engineering consultant at the Paris-based Margo consultancy, the group faces a number of choices.
They can carve Contracts out of the spec so the rest of C++26 can ship. That will be messy work, though. The undo button has to be smashed on a lot of library hardening already done using Contracts.
Another option is moving Contracts into a separate technical specification, where work can continue to refine the technology.
Or they could do a minor revision, vote again and hope the balmy Brazilian weather chills everyone out.®
d804e3b3819d0613: WASHINGTON: Microsoft said on Thursday that efforts to repair a major outage of Outlook were not going as expected and the firm was seeking alternative solutions as users around the world were left without its crucial services.
The hours-long disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, has hit email as well as products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
The impact of the outage has been felt globally, with users ranging from companies to governments reporting that they were unable to communicate via Outlook.
"We've monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected," Microsoft said on X.
"We're identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity," the tech giant added, without saying when service was expected to be fully restored.
The disruption went global within an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.
A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.

One of the impacted countries was New Zealand, where the foreign ministry sent a notice saying its "ability to receive emails has been affected by the global Microsoft outage. This also impacts all New Zealand Embassies, Consulates and Representative Offices around the world."
Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas", but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.
"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.
Downdetector, which tracks online outages, showed a sharp decline around 12.50 pm in users' reports of disruptions in Washington and Hong Kong.
Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.
As the outage dragged on for hours, Microsoft posted a series of updates on X, detailing continued but unsuccessful efforts to restore full service.
In one update shortly after 7am, Microsoft said it was "observing limited recovery" as it sought to route user traffic away from affected servers.
"As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect," the company added.
47c5281dc8bdbfb9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Backchannel political cooperation has not generated grassroots synergy for Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu in the Melaka state election, leaving an openly coordinated Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) pact on course to claim up to 24 seats, according to think tank Ilham Centre.

In a pre-polling study released on the eve of the vote, the research outfit found that the federal Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) between the Madani administration and Bersatu showed “little evidence of effectiveness” in forging voter-level alignment.
The firm noted that the arrangements conducted without open public messaging have alienated fence-sitters and left party loyalists adhering to traditional rivalries rather than pooling their votes.
The disconnect contrasts sharply with the formalised coordination achieved by BN and PN, which has synchronized grassroots campaign machinery and produced high vote transferability.

According to Ilham’s findings, 91 per cent of PN supporters expressed readiness to vote for BN candidates, while 78 per cent of BN voters were willing to back PN contenders. Under their shared electoral slate, BN is contesting 23 of Melaka’s 28 seats, with PN fielding candidates in the remaining five.
Ilham cautioned that in a first-past-the-post electoral system, vote splitting between parties sharing common political space provides an overwhelming structural advantage to unified opponents.

“PH and Bersatu must demonstrate greater political resolve in formalising an electoral alliance,” the firm said, warning that without formal agreements on candidate slates, seat quotas, common narratives, and integrated machinery, the partnership remains trapped as an “elite-level understanding”.
Based on stated voter preferences, Ilham projects the BN-PN alliance to lead in 24 constituencies, building upon the decisive majority BN secured in the 2021 state election when it claimed 21 seats.
Conversely, PH appears safe in only two urban strongholds, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, while its defensive battles in Ayer Keroh and Kesidang remain too close to call.

The report characterised PH’s support as “stable but stagnant”, noting that its appeal remains locked within non-Malay and urban precincts with negligible traction among Malay, rural, and undecided voters.

The survey gathered responses from 805 registered voters across all 28 constituencies between Nov 1 and 12 through stratified random sampling, supported by five focus group discussions and 22 in-depth interviews.

Carrying a statewide margin of error of 3.45 percentage points at a 95 per cent confidence level, the survey measures declared voting intent ahead of polling day tomorrow, Nov 14, following early voting on Nov 10.
dc77ea19f6c17ee7: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) recorded zero cases of sales exceeding the maximum price during the implementation of the Deepavali 2026 Festive Season Maximum Price Scheme (SHMMP) from November 4-10.

KPDN Enforcement director-general Datuk Azman Adam said the achievement reflected an improvement in trader compliance compared with last year, when six violations involving the sale of goods above the controlled prices were recorded.
“For this year, KPDN did not receive any complaints throughout the scheme’s implementation.
“This is a positive development compared with one complaint received at the retail level last year,” he said in a statement today.
He said that, overall, the number of enforcement cases taken by the KPDN during the implementation of the Deepavali 2026 SHMMP increased to 482, compared with 445 last year.
“Of the total, 481 cases involved the retail sector and one the wholesale sector, compared with 444 retail cases and one wholesale case last year,” he added.
Azman said the total compound value recorded this year decreased to RM50,800 compared with RM53,500 in 2025, while the value of seized goods also declined to RM14,045 from RM16,078 the previous year.
He said the majority of the offences detected involved traders failing to display the special pink price tags, with 481 cases recorded this year compared with 433 in 2025.
As for offences involving failure to display price tags, there was a significant drop as only one case was recorded compared to six last year.

“KPDN would like to express its appreciation to all parties involved throughout the implementation of the SHMMP this year, which resulted in zero cases of offences involving the sale of goods above the stipulated maximum prices,” he added. — Bernama
3f7e71b3edbae655: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan akan mempercepat usaha menangani banjir berulang di Selangor, termasuk menambah peruntukan serta meningkatkan kekerapan kerja pembersihan parit dan sungai.

Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim, berkata tindakan itu perlu diselaraskan segera antara semua jabatan berkaitan dengan kerajaan negeri bagi mengurangkan beban penduduk yang terpaksa berdepan banjir berulang kali.
Katanya, beliau tidak dapat menerima keadaan apabila penduduk terpaksa berdepan banjir sehingga empat atau lima kali setahun, meskipun paras air tidak terlalu tinggi.
“Hasil pertemuan saya dengan menteri-menteri dan kerajaan Selangor semalam, saya bermesyuarat di Parlimen kerana masalah yang dihadapi kesan banjir berterusan.

“Saya tidak boleh terima apabila penduduk terpaksa berdepan banjir empat hingga lima kali setahun. Walaupun paras air tidak tinggi, kesannya tetap membebankan rakyat,” katanya selepas menunaikan solat Jumaat di Madrasathul Gouthiyyah, Brickfields.

Anwar berkata, antara langkah perlu dipercepat ialah meningkatkan kekerapan pembersihan parit dan sungai, seperti dilaksanakan Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur (DBKL) yang kini menjalankan kerja itu enam kali setahun berbanding dua kali sebelum ini.
Beliau turut mengarahkan semua jabatan berkaitan, termasuk Jabatan Pengairan dan Saliran (JPS), memulakan tindakan segera tanpa menangguhkan kerja yang sudah dipersetujui.
Katanya, meskipun hujan lebat dan peningkatan paras air laut sukar dikawal, usaha tambahan perlu dilakukan bagi mengurangkan risiko banjir serta beban penduduk.
Dalam pada itu, Anwar berkata bantuan kepada mangsa banjir ditingkatkan daripada RM1,000 kepada RM2,500, manakala sumbangan kerajaan Selangor dinaikkan daripada RM500 kepada RM3,000.

Bagaimanapun, beliau menegaskan bantuan kewangan sahaja tidak mencukupi untuk mengatasi kesukaran mangsa, sebaliknya langkah pencegahan dan penyelenggaraan infrastruktur perlu dipertingkat secara berterusan.
Semalam, jumlah mangsa banjir di Selangor terus meningkat dengan dua lagi pusat pemindahan sementara (PPS) dibuka.
Di Kuala Selangor, jumlah mangsa di tujuh PPS meningkat kepada 1,180 orang daripada 330 keluarga berbanding 1,032 orang daripada 289 keluarga pada petang kelmarin.
5f8aef5b3eeda99b: PETALING JAYA: Kerjasama kerajaan serta Bersatu menerusi perjanjian keyakinan dan perbekalan (CSA) dilihat gagal membentuk persefahaman politik dalam kalangan pengundi Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan parti itu pada PRN Melaka, menurut Ilham Centre.
Badan pemikir itu berkata, kerjasama di belakang tabir tanpa hubungan politik secara terbuka menyebabkan hala tuju kesepakatan kedua-dua pihak tidak difahami akar umbi.

"Pendekatan kerjasama secara 'malu-malu' ini mewujudkan ketaksaan (kekaburan) dalam kalangan pengundi fence sitter (berkecuali) yang tidak dapat mengenal pasti hubungan sebenar antara kedua-dua entiti politik."
Menurutnya, ketiadaan mesej bersama menyebabkan penyokong PH dan Bersatu terus bergerak berdasarkan kesetiaan parti masing-masing, tanpa dorongan jelas untuk menyatukan sokongan mereka.

Sehubungan itu, Ilham Centre berpandangan PH dan Bersatu perlu memuktamadkan pakatan pilihan raya secara rasmi sekiranya mahu menjadikan kerjasama tersebut sebagai strategi menghadapi Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Perikatan Nasional (PN).

"Tanpa kesepakatan jelas dari segi calon, pembahagian kerusi, naratif dan mobilisasi jentera, kerjasama politik sedemikian berisiko kekal sebagai persefahaman elit yang gagal diterjemahkan kepada undi."
Kerajaan pada 29 Okt lalu memeterai CSA dengan 13 Ahli Parlimen, iaitu enam wakil rakyat Bersatu yang diketuai Muhyiddin Yassin dan Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Perjanjian itu merangkumi sokongan terhadap Belanjawan 2027 serta reformasi institusi, dengan wakil rakyat terbabit menerima peruntukan pembangunan kawasan setara Ahli Parlimen kerajaan.
Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim, sebelum ini menegaskan kawasan pembangkang tidak dipinggirkan daripada projek pembangunan kerajaan, namun mekanisme peruntukan melalui Ahli Parlimen perlu dirunding.

Polemik CSA mengundang kecaman Presiden PAS, Hadi Awang yang menyifatkannya 'pendekatan dajal', sedangkan parti itu pernah menganggotai kerajaan Ismail Sabri Yaakob yang memeterai memorandum persefahaman (MoU) dengan PH pada 13 Sept 2021 bagi menjamin kestabilan politik.

Timbalan Presiden PAS, Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, pula berpandangan CSA tidak wajar dijadikan budaya politik baharu kerana seolah-olah tidak mengiktiraf pilihan rakyat, selain berpotensi menyemarakkan salah guna kuasa demi mendapatkan sokongan.
Moral jentera BN tinggi, PH hilang rentak

Ilham Centre mendapati moral jentera BN berada pada tahap tinggi susulan kejayaan PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan, manakala naratif politik identiti menerusi slogan 'Asal Bukan PH' semakin mendapat tempat sepanjang kempen.

Sebaliknya, PH dilihat gagal menyatukan isu rasuah, kesenjangan ekonomi dan skandal tadbir urus sebagai naratif induk yang mampu membangkitkan gelombang penolakan terhadap BN, selain kempen yang banyak bergantung kepada kekuatan calon di kawasan masing-masing.
"Ketiadaan naratif induk menyebabkan kempen PH bergerak secara terpisah mengikut calon dan kawasan tanpa mesej politik yang benar-benar mencengkam imaginasi pengundi."

Penilaian Ilham Centre itu berdasarkan kajian lapangan dari 1 hingga 12 Nov lalu membabitkan 805 responden merentasi semua 28 DUN Melaka, dengan dapatan turut disokong perbincangan kumpulan berfokus dan temu bual mendalam.

07152e79d08ec382: TELUK INTAN: A retired teacher pleaded not guilty in the sessions court here today to 17 charges of physically sexually assaulting seven female students aged 13 to 15, between May 2024 and July 7 last year.
Zaidi Abbas, 56, who is physically disabled, made the plea after the charges were read out to him before judge Rafidah Che Aziz.
He was charged with committing the offences while holding a position of trust as a teacher.

The offences were alleged to have taken place in a special room and the canteen of a secondary school in Langkap, as well as in a vehicle in the surrounding area and during a journey back from Teluk Intan.
The charges were framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16(1) of the same Act.

The offences carry a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction. The court may also impose an additional prison sentence of between two and five years, together with at least two strokes of the cane.
Deputy public prosecutor Izzuddin Fakri Hamdan offered bail of RM70,000 for all the charges with the additional conditions.

However, lawyer Koh Shean Wai, representing Zaidi, appealed for the bail amount to be reduced to RM1,000 for each charge on the grounds that his client, who was earning about RM4,000 a month, had to support his wife, mother and four school-going children.
He said Zaidi did not have a criminal record and was not a flight risk.

Rafidah granted bail of RM40,000 for all 17 charges, and also ordered Zaidi not to intimidate the victims, as well as to report to the nearest police station once a month pending disposal of the case.
The court fixed Dec 14 for mention and submission of documents.

85a581e61908684a: PETALING JAYA: Umno today proposed four options for DAP to consider in light of its dissatisfaction over former prime minister Najib Razak’s house arrest, which took effect on Tuesday.
In a lengthy statement, Umno information chief Azalina Othman Said said the first recourse for DAP would be to seek mediation among the unity government’s component parties.

She said Clause 5(c) of the unity government’s agreement provides for mediation through a consultative council, comprising representatives from the coalitions’ components, to resolve any disputes or misunderstandings.
However, Azalina found it “curious” that DAP did not seek mediation earlier despite the fact that the subject of Najib’s pardon had been public knowledge since January 2024.
She said the second recourse would be terminating the agreement.
However, no such clause exists in the agreement, as it is intended to last until the end of the 15th Parliament.
“Therefore, the obvious conclusion here would be for the dissolution of Parliament.”

Azalina said the third option was for DAP to remain calm and allow the existing arrangements to continue, noting that the party benefited from “the royal prerogative of mercy in 2018”, alluding to then opposition leader Anwar Ibrahim’s royal pardon and the king’s intervention in 2022 that facilitated the formation of the unity government.
“This underscores the importance of respecting both the constitutional role and the royal prerogative of mercy.”

Finally, DAP could also seek a review of the unity government’s agreement, specifically Paragraph C, which deals with the affirmation by the components to uphold the Federal Constitution, including the institution of the Malay Rulers.
“Any consideration by DAP to review Paragraph C would bring unanticipated consequences to the continuity of the unity government.”
Azalina’s comments follow DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo’s challenge for Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to resign if he did not support Anwar’s prime ministership.

Gobind’s remarks were in response to Zahid’s statement on Tuesday that dissolving Parliament would be preferable to a Cabinet reshuffle, following DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook’s resignation as transport minister.
Loke resigned in September over Najib’s conditional pardon, but it only took effect after the former Pekan MP began his house arrest earlier this week.
Azalina said Gobind’s statement was “regrettable” and did little to strengthen the spirit of cooperation within the unity government.
She added that issuing public ultimatums to the president of a coalition partner is neither constructive nor consistent with the spirit of the unity government's agreement.
"If there are differences of opinion among coalition partners, the appropriate response is dialogue and consultation, not public pressure or demands for resignation.”
She also said that the party will continue to honour its commitments, respect Anwar's leadership and uphold the Federal Constitution.
"We have made our position clear. The next move is yours.”
7dfac5c4209c9554: In Australia, they’re calling it the “Microsoft long weekend” – an outage so pervasive it’s just about made Friday a write-off at organizations which rely on Redmond’s online services, especially Exchange Online.

As The Register reported yesterday, the outage started on Thursday at around 18:00 UTC and saw Microsoft 365 users unable to access email, attend Teams meetings, use cloud PCs, consult Copilot, or enjoy full access to another 15 hosted services.
The software giant says the outage impacts Microsoft 365 services “that interact with Exchange Online and email services.” Services that don’t need Exchange Online remain functional.
The software giant initially blamed the outage on a mysterious “problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.”
Microsoft thought it found a fix but quickly admitted “Actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief.”
In the hours since, the situation has not improved markedly, and Microsoft is still struggling to restore service.
It has also changed the language it uses when discussing the possibility that a cyberattack is the reason for the outage.

As of 04:11 UTC, the company said it could find “no indication this is the result of malicious activity.” An update time-stamped 05:46 UTC stated “As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident.”

Microsoft’s status page preserves only the company’s most recent update, but its RSS feed preserves each missive. That feed tells a tale of woe that we have distilled into lowlights and present in chronological order:
We’re applying infrastructure capacity improvements where possible in an effort to help support traffic in regions coming online;
We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed that change is not taking as expected;

We’re reviewing traffic flows and affected infrastructure to identify opportunities to optimize routing. This includes verifying the reasons for service failures so we can develop specific actions to improve stability;
We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances;
We're observing partial recovery across regions in which we've applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren't resulting in sustained recovery;

Current actions we are taking include scaling up virtual machines to increase capacity and reduce load. However, we are encountering issues with the machines being stuck in a bad state, preventing our changes from syncing as expected.
Microsoft’s latest status update doesn’t suggest this will be over any time soon.

“We’re continuing to pursue multiple workstreams to pinpoint the underlying cause of the traffic influx and advance the recoverability of the backend servers,” Microsoft wrote. “We’re taking a measured approach to identify and repair affected infrastructure to improve the ability to confirm the developed changes were applied. We’re tracking the results of this approach to verify the servers are showing the anticipated recovery and performance intended.”
Hopefully, Australia and other countries in nearby time zones won’t be the only ones to get an unscheduled long weekend. ®

d9dc5db21bdd63b1: Working in tech support can be thankless when gormless colleagues leave you sleepless. Which is why, each Friday, The Register runs a new instalment of On Call – the reader contributed column which ensures your work to keep tech alive doesn't remain unnoticed.
This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Tim" who told that while working for a phone company he once rewrote 2,650 lines of C as a six line shell script.
He performed that feat after being asked to fix a data transfer program that, strangely, included a bespoke implementation of the venerable File Transfer Protocol (FTP).
"Writing the script took eight hours, most of it tracking down the source code of FTP so I could see if it would do what I wanted," Tim wrote.

This story took place before the World Wide Web became the way to find information online. To find the code he needed, Tim therefore used a Wide Area Information Server (WAIS) to search remote databases.

"In those days, there was no Linux and AT&T had licensed the Unix source code to universities with the struct proviso that it never be made publicly available," Tim explained. "It took me quite some time using WAIS to track it down – the security could have been better – and read the code."
Having found what he needed, Tim wrote his script, which ran overnight to collect data from the telco's switches, tidied up the raw info, and uploaded it to a mainframe.
"It would automatically page me if it couldn't connect to a switch or mainframe after three attempts," he explained.
The script worked fine, but the telco's networks didn't. Tim's pager was soon going off two or three times a night, every night.
After two weeks of interrupted sleep, Tim's manager kindly told him to give the pager to a colleague.
But that colleague habitually left the pager at work, forgot to turn it on, or conveniently placed it out of earshot.
So Tim reluctantly took back the pager and endured another few weeks of nightly interruptions.
How many consecutive sleepless nights have you endured while On Call? If you have enough energy, click here to send your story with On Call so we can share it on a future Friday. ®

"The market fears that after Huang's resignation, Nvidia will reduce sourcing from Chinese suppliers," said Wu Zhou, fund manager at Shenzhen Deyuan Investment Co.
"The US will also likely tighten restrictions on China's access to advanced chips, including the renting of offshore cloud computing power."
Wu said such a prospect bodes ill for AI firms that desperately need computing power, but benefits homegrown AI chipmakers.

Domestic chipmaker Hygon Information Technology was poised to gain 7% this week.

US House Speaker Mike Johnson ​said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after the scandal.

Meanwhile, Chinese AI companies are trying to rent ​Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China, worried that the development around Nvidia's Huang could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their remote use of ‌advanced processors.

"The biggest risk to China's AI industry is that the scandal leads to a tightening of US export controls on advanced chips and chip-making equipment, possibly by the end of this year," Gavekal Dragonomics said in a report.

Huang was the most influential opponent of tight chip export controls to China, so his scandal, "combined with the arrival of a more AI-skeptical Congress, will make it ever harder for Chinese AI companies to gain access to the advanced compute they so desperately crave," the think tank said.

“If the US government tighten Chinese access to US chips, we expect all the companies with LLM business will be negatively impacted,” Chelsey Tam, senior equity analyst at Morningstar, said, referring to Chinese AI model firms.

c158ddc68ac550a1: WASHINGTON: Microsoft said on Thursday that efforts to repair a major outage of Outlook were not going as expected and the firm was seeking alternative solutions as users around the world were left without its crucial services.
The hours-long disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, has hit email as well as products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
The impact of the outage has been felt globally, with users ranging from companies to governments reporting that they were unable to communicate via Outlook.
"We've monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected," Microsoft said on X.
"We're identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity," the tech giant added, without saying when service was expected to be fully restored.
The disruption went global within an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.
A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.

One of the impacted countries was New Zealand, where the foreign ministry sent a notice saying its "ability to receive emails has been affected by the global Microsoft outage. This also impacts all New Zealand Embassies, Consulates and Representative Offices around the world."
Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas" but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.
"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.
Downdetector, which tracks online outages, showed a sharp decline around 0450 GMT in users' reports of disruptions in Washington and Hong Kong.
Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.
As the outage dragged on for hours, Microsoft posted a series of updates on X, detailing continued but unsuccessful efforts to restore full service.
In one update shortly after 6pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT), Microsoft said it was "observing limited recovery" as it sought to route user traffic away from affected servers.
"As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect," the company added.

606399e29c9ee7e9: The use of algorithms to design structures has led to new parts optimized for ultralight aircraft, high-bandwidth antennas, and F1 racing cars. But the best algorithmic design techniques still require lots of computation and time: Users only see the final design after it’s complete, after which they often must start the design process all over again to make changes. That process also makes it harder to trust that the final designs are structurally sound. MIT researchers are making algorithmic designs more collaborative with a system that acts like an AI copilot. As the algorithm is generating the structure, it presents regions to the human designer for feedback. In an open-access Communications Engineering paper describing the system, the researchers showed it led to more easily manufacturable structures with higher buckling loads while adding only 15 seconds to the total design time compared to all-algorithmic approaches. The researchers believe the approach, which uses a design technique known as topology optimization, could make algorithmic design more accessible and manufacturable for a broader class of design engineers. “Right now, the human doesn’t have any agency or control over the design process as it’s playing out,” explains lead author Dat Ha PhD ’26, a recent MIT civil and environmental engineering doctoral student who is now a structural designer at LeMessurier. “For these really complex designs, we wanted to also tap into our brain, which is the most complex machine there is, to solve these design problems in a way that’s more practical to industry.” Joining Ha on the paper are Ferdous Alam, a former MIT postdoc who is now an assistant professor at Georgia Tech; Markus Buehler, the MIT Jerry McAfee (1940) Professor of Engineering; Faez Ahmed, MIT associate professor of mechanical engineering; and senior author Josephine Carstensen, MIT associate professor of civil and environmental engineering. Bringing a human in the loop Topology optimization is one of the most advanced and promising algorithmic design techniques. It uses formal optimization techniques to iteratively fill in the space given for a design in a way that maximally achieves the stated goals. For most applications, the process requires a lot of computation and time. When it’s finally done, the designs can be impractical to build or have other issues the engineer didn’t consider. For instance, some designs might have eight or more beam connections at a single point, which would be difficult to make in the real world. “Engineers are always very skeptical of computer programs, especially if they give you very weird-looking or unexpected designs,” Ha says. “On paper, topology optimization is really powerful and can achieve great, high-performing designs, but its black box nature has made it less widely adopted in industry.” Topology optimization has gotten traction in the automotive and aerospace industries, but it’s been used less to design buildings or bridges, partly because design engineers need to know they can trust the output. “A big limiting factor has been that the design engineer has very little influence over how the design evolves and therefore can’t control undesirable features,” Carstensen explains. “The lack of control and lack of ownership also inhibits its use.” To address those problems, the researchers made topology optimization more collaborative in an approach that Carstensen compares to having a design copilot. Prior attempts at adding human judgment slowed things down dramatically. The researchers’ new system uses machine learning to quickly identify the most likely regions of an algorithmic design that a human would want to change. To train the machine-learning model, the researchers created a synthetic dataset of probable human feedback to thousands of designs that critiqued things like aesthetics, performance criteria, and manufacturability. “We thought if we could create a record of where humans have made changes to these programs, then perhaps there’s a pattern to those choices, which is not very different from other types of machine-learning approaches,” Ha says. Carstensen sees the system as bringing together the best of algorithmic and human design approaches. “The idea is to tap into the brains of the designers and get them to infuse their domain knowledge as the design evolves,” Carstensen says. In demonstrations, the researchers showed their human-in-the-loop approach improved manufacturability and linear buckling load by 39 percent while only modestly increasing the total design time. Right now, the approach only allows users to make structures within identified regions thicker or thinner, but they hope to add other options for modification in future versions. “The hope is that by addressing these hurdles, we open up topology optimization to a much wider audience, not only in industry but also to researchers and students in academia,” Carstensen says. From designs to structures The researchers see their approach complementing AI only-approaches to design. “We are arguing there’s room for both,” Carstensen says. “If you are in a discipline that has a lot of computational resources, you can use the other approach. But if you really need the human input, you can use this collaborative approach.” Adding human input also serves to increase trust. “In some settings, the humans need to make the final decisions before advancing the final design,” Carstensen says. “By involving humans, we can get higher-performing designs to the real world to create higher-performing structures. Because it’s not just about designing good artifacts; it’s about creating good artifacts that humans will actually accept and make.” The work was supported, in part, by the MathWorks Engineering Fellowship Fund, TATA Steel, and the MIT Generative AI Impact Consortium.
666c9ce2ae9f1142: Despite fears about robots replacing humans at work, there are still plenty of things humans can do far better than machines. That’s fine with Robust AI, a startup building robots designed to complement what humans do best. The company’s mobile robot, named Carter, resembles a utility cart on wheels and is designed to fit seamlessly alongside humans in fast-changing warehouse and factory environments. Carter features a force-sensitive handlebar for easy guidance, an AI-powered vision system, and holonomic wheels for instant movement in any direction. As a result, humans can cut Carter off, push and pull it in any direction with one hand, and direct it with gestures or the onboard touch screen. The company’s robots are currently deployed in logistics warehouses and on factory floors, where they help humans while picking or stocking shelves and moving items across facilities autonomously. “In these environments, what really determines success is how the overall system performs,” explains Anthony Jules ’92, SM ’92, who co-founded the company with MIT Professor Emeritus Rodney Brooks. “The robot does some of the work, the people do some of the work, and the backend systems do some of the work. It’s that combination that determines how well your system performs. We believe it’s really important that people have an appropriate level of agency and input so that they’re always moving the system forward.” Collaborative robots Brooks was a faculty member at MIT from 1984 until 2010 and served as the director of the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) from 1997 until 2007. While at MIT, he co-founded iRobot, which invented the popular Roomba vacuum and went public in 2005. Later, he co-founded the company Rethink Robotics, which also designed collaborative robots. Jules met Brooks as a graduate student at CSAIL in the 1990s. The two never worked together, but their labs were on the same floor. The pair kept in touch after Jules graduated and co-founded the company Sapient, which went public before being acquired by Publicis in 2015. In 2019, Brooks bumped into Jules at a robotics conference. He told Jules he was thinking of starting a robotics software company, which he compared to a video game engine for training robots. Robust AI was founded later that year. The Covid-19 pandemic caused the founders to shift to creating robots that could autonomously disinfect surfaces, but when it was discovered that Covid-19 was not transmitted via surfaces, they had to pivot again. “That forced us to decide how to use this technology we had been building, which was really about helping robots understand the world more fully,” Jules recalls. “Long story short, I said to Rodney, ‘I have an idea. You’re going to love it and you’re going to hate it. You’re going to love it because it’s solving problems for customers that we’ve been hearing about, and you’re going to hate it because we have to build hardware.” The founders had been interviewing potential customers for years through Robust AI’s early pivots. They finally decided on logistics and manufacturing as the industries to target early on. “When people think about automation in factories, they think about pictures of the 5 percent that are fully automated with $50 to $200 million dollar systems,” says Jules, who now serves as Robust AI’s chief innovation officer. “They don’t think about the vast majority of factories that aren’t automated at all. These factories don’t even have a conveyor belt. They are not going to tear everything out and replace it with a $200 million system.” Robust AI’s robots can be phased into operations as needed and offer several workflows for customers. In one workflow, the robot can guide human workers to specific spaces to retrieve items. In another it can follow humans to important spots for loading. The primary workflows involve Carter robots moving things from one place to another, often in large warehouses or factories, where they say human workers can walk on average 30,000 steps a day. “These are huge spaces, so a person might load the robot with things and then need to bring them to another station, but that could be 400 feet away,” says, Brooks, Robust AI’s chief technology officer. “Now the person can just say ‘done’ and the robot brings it instead. How the robots are integrated into the workspace is entirely up to the customer.” Getting work done Leila Takayama, Robust AI’s vice president of human robot interaction, recently discovered a peer-reviewed study of robots in hospitals, which were used to do things like gather dishes, move sheets, and transport other equipment. The researchers discovered that, in many hospitals, a large number of robots were turned off and against the walls. The nurses said they broke. “What really happened was the nurses were rushing with a patient on a gurney, and the robot sees them in the hallway and stops dead, and they couldn’t get the gurney around them,” Brooks says. “The robots were getting in the way of nurses’ primary tasks.” Robust AI’s approach to technology development is to understand workers’ primary tasks deeply and build features that accelerate those tasks, whether a human or a robot is doing them. “We let humans do what humans are good at in the physical world, which we’ve had millions of years of evolution to get good at, and have the digital system respond to that and provide us with all the things that it is good at,” Brooks explains.

c3a1e49c87d8788a: The government of Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs has revealed it investigated Alice Huang, the woman who is an alleged Chinese intelligence asset and had an intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and a possible entanglement with troubled server-maker Supermicro. US authorities provided only “limited assistance” in the matter, despite Singapore asking for help.
The Ministry outlined its activities in a statement published late on Thursday, Singapore time.
The document reveals that Singapore’s Police Force (SPF) and Customs agency commenced an investigation into Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, in February 2025.

“The suspected domestic offences pertained to potential false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers and other related offences,” the Ministry wrote, adding that the exec “was not investigated for espionage.”
Singaporean authorities wanted to know if servers bought by local companies, but exported to Malaysia without ever touching Singaporean soil, might have ended up in a third country.

It is not unusual for Singapore-based companies to acquire goods that never reach the island, because it promotes itself as the ideal spot from which to run an operation that trades across Asia. Singapore does so because it is tiny – the whole nation is the same size as the five boroughs of New York City.
That small size means Singapore restricts the number of datacenters that can operate on its soil.
Those limits are a big reason why Malaysia’s Johor region, which is under 20kms from the border with Singapore and a joint special economic zone, has become a major datacenter province.
Singapore needs deals like that to thrive but works hard to ensure its hospitality is not abused.
Which is why it felt Megaspeed’s activities worthy of investigation.

US authorities were interested too. On 24 June 2025, the Bureau of Industry and Security, which regulates sensitive goods subject to export controls, visited Megaspeed in Singapore to check the hardware it bought arrived at its intended destination.
Ms. Huang attended that event and later met the SPF for an interview.
That meeting ended with the SPF impounding her passport, so it could keep her in Singapore while the investigation continued.
As the matter progressed, the SPF suspected perennially troubled server-maker Supermicro had a role in this situation.

Readers may recall that the US Department of Justice indicted two Supermicro execs for conspiring to ship servers to China in contravention of US law. Supermicro investigated the matter and parted ways with three staff who acted improperly. The company has denied ever selling to Megaspeed.
Singaporean authorities say they received only “limited cooperation” from Supermicro, so in July 2025 the office of the nation’s Attorney General asked US authorities for help.

“Since September 2025, SPF has repeated this request on several occasions to the US Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigation,” the statement reveals. “Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company.”

In February 2026, the SPF “concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated.”
But the police did decide that Ms. Huang provided inaccurate information “to downplay her role in Megaspeed.”
“She was issued a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country.”
The police returned her passport and Ms. Huang left Singapore on the same day.
The Singaporean statement shows the island nation wants the world to know it does not facilitate sanction-busting activity and takes even the hint of it seriously.

That matters to Nvidia, too, because Singaporean buyers sometimes account for over 20 percent of its quarterly revenue and may continue to do so. Whoever replaces Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO will surely face many questions about the company’s practices. Singapore may just have made answering those queries a little easier. ®
